Ready To Build Something Real?

John Galt Services seeks a full-time AI-Native Full-Stack TypeScript Engineer to serve TWO US customers at the same time, splitting your time evenly between them:

• A medical business: a healthcare-technology company that runs a Salesforce-based platform for bariatric surgery programs.

• A hospitality business: a group operating a restaurant, a historic wedding venue, and a planned hotel.

Each customer runs its own dedicated AI platform instance: an assistant that lives in their Slack, reads their email and meetings, and writes and runs software on their behalf. Your job is to make both platforms deliver. You'll connect them to each customer's systems, turn real business pain points into dependable automations, and build the tools each business needs, almost all of it in TypeScript, front end to back end.
You won't be maintaining a legacy codebase nobody cares about. Both are small, founder-led operations with more ideas than engineering hands, and most of what you build will be new. You'll need to switch cleanly between two very different businesses and keep both happy.
You must be fluent in English. You will join our customers' teams as a remote member with real responsibilities, not busywork.

IMPORTANT!

Your application is our first test of your attention to detail and ability to follow instructions. 👀
👉 Read this ENTIRE job listing!
👉 Follow the application instructions EXACTLY!

👉 If you do not meet the minimum qualifications for the job, DO NOT APPLY!

If you fail to follow the instructions below, we will reject your application without reading it!

Minimum Job Qualifications

FLUENT SPOKEN & WRITTEN ENGLISH! You will communicate daily with a US-based team. Your English must be clear and confident, spoken and written. If you aren't sure, keep practicing and apply next time.
REAL SOFTWARE DEVELOPMENT EXPERIENCE! We hire experienced developers who haven't yet made the leap to senior. You have years of real development behind you, not just coursework. You are comfortable across the stack: web front end, back-end services, and the API integrations that connect them.
SOLID TYPESCRIPT SKILLS! This is a TypeScript-intensive role, and your interview will dig deep into it. You must understand and value type safety: modelling a domain in types, using generics where they earn their keep, and keeping the compiler on your side. If your instinct is to slap any on everything and "fix it later," this isn't the right fit. You should have built real front-end AND back-end code in TypeScript, including Node.js back-end services.

REAL REACT EXPERIENCE! The front ends you build will be React. You must have shipped real React applications in TypeScript: components, hooks, state management, and talking to a back-end API. A tutorial to-do app does not count.

A PUBLIC GITHUB HISTORY! We will look at your GitHub profile before we look at anything else. Show us what you've built, especially your open-source contributions. If your GitHub is empty, this isn't the right fit.

CURIOSITY ABOUT AGENTIC CODING! You will do much of your work through an AI platform that writes code alongside you. It takes a couple of weeks to get fluent. If you think AI coding tools are a gimmick, or you expect them to do your thinking for you, keep looking.

YOU CAN SERVE TWO MASTERS! You'll be juggling two customers with different businesses, systems, and priorities. You must keep their work and data separate, split your time evenly between them, and switch context without dropping balls.

SELF-DIRECTED OWNERSHIP! You'll work with integrations you've never seen before: Salesforce, Atlassian, Google Workspace, QuickBooks, point-of-sale systems. You won't be expected to know them on day one, but you'll be expected to dig in and figure them out. If you need someone looking over your shoulder at every step, this role will be frustrating for both of us.

A DISCIPLINED ENGINEERING APPROACH! You test what you build. You read the requirements before you code. You document your work. You don't push to main and pray. We don't expect perfection. We DO expect professionalism.

You MUST have at least a Bachelor degree.

You MUST be willing to work late night hours.

You MUST either live on Bali or be willing to relocate to Bali.

You MUST have the right to work legally in Indonesia. JGS does NOT sponsor work visas!

ATTENTION TO DETAIL! The moment we see your application, we'll know.

If you do not meet ALL of these requirements, DO NOT APPLY for this job!

Nice To Have

• Salesforce development (Apex, Lightning, Salesforce APIs). Not required, but this is the experience we want most. The medical customer's product is built on Salesforce, and Salesforce skills will put you at the front of the line.

• AWS platform experience, especially serverless application development (e.g. Lambda, API Gateway, DynamoDB)

• REST API integrations with third-party SaaS platforms

• Atlassian Jira & Bitbucket, Slack and Google Workspace APIs

• AI coding tools and LLM-based workflows

• Multi-tenant SaaS architecture

• Healthcare data or HIPAA-aware development

• QuickBooks, accounting, or point-of-sale integrations

• Hospitality, restaurant, or inventory systems

What You'll Do

For both customers:

• Platform ownership: Configure and maintain each customer's AI platform instance and keep its integrations healthy.

• Automation engineering: Turn recurring business processes into dependable, scripted jobs, including automated expense monitoring that catches cost anomalies before they add up.

• Documentation: Document what you build so it can be understood and maintained.

For the medical customer:

• Integrate with Slack, Google Workspace, Atlassian, and Salesforce.

• Automate work like document-to-CRM data entry, marketing-content pipelines, and executive briefings.

• Build front-end and back-end tools alongside the customer's existing developer, and help prototype new product ideas.

For the hospitality customer:

• Connect point-of-sale systems through their APIs or through QuickBooks.

• Automate expense tracking and restaurant inventory management.

• Research the customer's existing systems and work out how to integrate them.

Reporting Structure

You report to each customer's owner, who sets day-to-day priorities for their share of your time. You coordinate technical work with each customer's existing technical staff. John Galt Services provides technical direction, architectural guidance, and mentoring.
Working Arrangements

You are supporting our customers remotely, but this is NOT a remote job! We will provide working space and equipment near Canggu, Bali. All work is performed on-site.
Salary & Benefits

New associates start at a probationary pay scale of IDR 8 jt / month gross (i.e. before taxes & benefits). Your probationary period is three months.
After successfully completing probation, you become eligible for placement and performance bonuses that can significantly increase your total compensation:

• Placement Bonus: Up to IDR 4,000,000/month when placed with clients, bringing your effective monthly compensation to IDR 12 jt / month gross.

• Performance Bonus: Up to 50% of your total monthly compensation (base + placement bonus) for any month in which you meet or exceed expectations. This can bring your total pay as high as IDR 18 jt / month gross.

We also reserve a large pool of funds for staff perks, events & annual bonuses. If we are happy with your work, you will be VERY happy with your choice!
Also, our office is just minutes from the beach, right outside Canggu, Bali. If you know, you know!
Growth Path

You are the first engineer on what we expect to become a team. Both customers have more ideas than engineering capacity, and as the work outgrows one person, additional engineers will join. When that happens, you have a clear path to graduate into the team lead role: setting technical direction, mentoring the engineers who join after you, and owning delivery across both customers.
Who Is John Galt?

Good question! Might help to show up at your interview with an answer.
HOW TO APPLY 👈

Make sure your JobStreet profile includes a valid email & WhatsApp phone number.
Include this EXACT cover letter:
It must be written in fluent English, BY YOU, not by an AI assistant. We can tell! 👀

The very top line of the cover letter should contain ONLY a link to your GitHub profile. Nothing else.

Below this, describe your experience as a TypeScript developer: your React front-end work, your back-end work, and any integration or automation work.

If you have ANY Salesforce experience (Apex, Lightning, Salesforce APIs, or administration), tell us about it. What did you build, and on what kind of org? If you have none, say so.

There will be thousands of applicants for this job. Explain why we should pick YOU.

Kulu builds an AI agent that joins live meetings — it listens, speaks, sees the user's shared screen, and takes actions in real time. Everything runs on realtime infrastructure: WebRTC media, streaming LLM sessions, a Python backend, and the cloud underneath.

We're hiring an infrastructure engineer to run it with us. You'll join our Foundation team, reporting directly to the CTO, and your work will centre on three things in the first half year: migrating us from AWS to GCP, building our monitoring from the ground up, and keeping production healthy when things break.

We're a small, high-bandwidth team, deliberately building toward a more in-person culture in Bali.

Tasks

• Design, build, and maintain the realtime platform Kulu's AI assistant runs on — WebRTC media infrastructure, streaming multimodal LLM sessions, and the Python backend behind them: the foundation every user conversation rides on.

• Own reliability, performance, and observability of Kulu's core services: the realtime pipeline end to end — rooms, agents, audio in/out, and the recording pipeline — and the telemetry that turns the agent felt slow into a number with a cause.

• Own the LLM streaming session layer as an engineering system — connection lifecycle, streaming, reconnection and resumption, tool-call plumbing, timeouts and watchdogs — so that behaviour changes designed by the AI product lead land on a reliable substrate.

• Own deployment and infrastructure across our AWS environment and CI/CD pipelines, and drive our infrastructure-as-code programme (OpenTofu).

• Maintain the platform in production and respond to incidents: triage, root-cause, and fix live issues across the stack, then feed every incident back into telemetry, runbooks, and infrastructure as code so it can't happen silently twice.

• Build services that handle sensitive meeting data with the privacy, correctness, and auditability our customers expect.

• Contribute to architectural decisions as Kulu scales, with a particular focus on system correctness, data integrity, and security.

• Bring strong engineering fundamentals to every problem: well-tested, maintainable code, clear data models, and systems that degrade gracefully under pressure.

• Maintain strong documentation and champion operational excellence across the engineering culture.

• Ship end to end: you write the migration, deploy the service, and watch the dashboards after.

Requirements

• 3+ years of production experience in a DevOps, SRE, Cloud Engineer, Platform Engineer, or backend infrastructure role.

• Production experience writing and owning infrastructure as code (Terraform/OpenTofu).

• Knowledge of monitoring and logging tooling (Prometheus/Grafana, Datadog, ELK, or equivalent).

• Strong programming skills in Python (asyncio, FastAPI or similar) and solid shell scripting (Bash).

• Solid operational experience with AWS or GCP — ideally some of both, since your first project is migrating us from one to the other — including IAM, secrets management, VPC and networking.

• Hands-on experience building CI/CD pipelines (GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, or similar); proficiency with Git and branching strategies.

• Strong grasp of distributed systems, event-driven architecture, and fault-tolerant service design.

• Solid relational database skills (PostgreSQL, schema migrations); Redis in production.

• Strong understanding of infrastructure and application security best practices.

• Strong AI-tool skills: AI is part of how you read, write, and debug code.

• Clear communicator; fluent spoken and written English — our company language is exclusively English.

Nice to Have

• AWS or GCP certifications (e.g., Solutions Architect, DevOps Engineer).

• Security compliance experience — supporting a certification programme (SOC 2 / ISO 42001), access management, or audit preparation.

• Experience supporting eval or model-quality infrastructure.

Our Stack

Python (FastAPI, asyncio) · WebRTC media infrastructure · streaming multimodal LLM APIs · PostgreSQL · Redis · React + TypeScript · AWS · GitHub Actions · OpenTofu · Datadog

Benefits
IDR 25–40m/month gross

What Success Looks Like

• First month: you can deploy, configure, and debug our infrastructure on your own, and the GCP migration plan is ready — target architecture chosen, quotas requested, steps written down.

• Three months: the migration is finished — our environments run on GCP, fully managed as code — the first dashboards and alerts are live, and when something breaks in production, you're the person who handles it.

• Six months: AWS is fully shut down; is production healthy is one look at a dashboard you built; incidents are diagnosed in minutes instead of hours; the team ships every week without worrying about infrastructure.

Our Operating Principles:

• Always Be Hustlin – Move fast, outwork the competition, stay scrappy.

• Relentlessly Curious – Reason from first principles, question assumptions and explore better ways.

• Super Pumped – Show relentless enthusiasm and drive.

• Make Magic – Create experiences that delight customers.

• Obsess Over the Details – Perfect the product experience, no matter how small.

• Big Bold Bets – Think big, take risks and go after huge, transformative opportunities.

• Ownership is Key – Own the outcome, not just the task.

As Kulu grows, this role naturally expands with the Foundation team — a full-stack engineer will join on Simu, and there is a clear path to owning our infrastructure and reliability function outright.

CHI 是一家自主化活动科技公司。一个小团队指挥 100+ 个 AI agent。我们正在招聘一位人类 operator，负责交付产品并运行其背后的基础设施。

CHI 运行 live event 的完整 stack：ticketing、cashless payments、POS、wristbands、vendor settlements、coupons、CRM 和 analytics，服务 festivals、venues 和大规模活动。

当我们的平台出问题时，成千上万的人买不了饮料。这就是我们所说的 “production” 级别。

CHI 被构建成一家自主化公司：一个小型人类团队指挥一支 AI agent workforce，执行所有可重复流程 — code、review、release、QA、on-call、support、reconciliation、fraud review 和 outreach。人类设定方向和品味；agents 执行。我们已经在内部证明：更小的团队能比它替代的组织快数倍 ship。

我们正在为这支 agent workforce 招聘一位人类 operator — 一名 AI-native engineer（dev + DevOps）。不是“偶尔用 AI”的人，而是会构建、优化和指挥 AI agents 及其 loops，把软件交付作为主要工作方式的人：product features、coding、testing、debugging、infrastructure、incident analysis 和 documentation，全都 agent-driven。你将是公司里少数人类之一，直接与 founders 合作，end to end 拥有真实系统 — 以及运行这些系统的 agents。
这里真实的一周，不是假设
• End to end ship 一个面向 organizer 的 feature — Postgres data model、NestJS API、React backstage UI、tests、release notes — 指挥 AI agents 穿过每一层，并对体验负责。
• 设计一个新的 ticketing 或 payments flow，真的会被数千名 attendees 使用 — 从 spec 到 app 和 POS 上线 — 然后在现场观察它。
• 通过 gateway、backend logs 和 provider dashboard 追踪一次失败的 card payment — 当天 ship fix 和 reconciliation script。
• 通过我们的 versioned pipeline 将变更从 PR 推到 production：conventional commit → automated release → OCI artifact → test → staging → production promotion。
• 构建一个 AI agent 或 CI workflow，用来 review PRs、run QA，或草拟 release notes 和 incident reports — 让团队不再手动做这些事。
• 响应 production incident — VM disk full、missed webhook — 修复、backfill data，并自动化下一次能捕获它的 check。
我们的 stack（真实版本）
• 后端: Node.js / TypeScript (NestJS), Bun
• 前端: React（organizer backstage + web apps）、PWA 和 native mobile
• 数据: PostgreSQL (WAL + PITR)、Redis、Kafka、Cassandra、YugabyteDB edge replication
• 基础设施: Dedicated Hetzner VMs 上的 Docker Compose。通过 Tailscale 做 zero-trust networking，并使用 hardened host firewalls。
• 网关与身份: KrakenD API gateway、Keycloak、HashiCorp Vault（agent templates、AppRole auth）
• 支付: Stripe Connect、Hyperswitch（PCI vault + cloud KMS）、Xendit、Stripe Terminal / tap-to-pay。真钱，真实 settlements。
• CI / CD: GitHub Actions（60+ workflows）、release-please、OCI config artifacts、gated test → staging → prod promotion
• 可观测性与安全: Grafana、Loki、Prometheus、Promtail、Wazuh HIDS、ClamAV — 在 PCI DSS scope 内运行
• AI 工具链: Custom coding agents、multi-agent workflows、MCP servers、Paperclip、Hermes agents、LiteLLM proxy、本地 / self-hosted LLMs

你不需要全都有经验。你需要是那种能快速上手任何部分的 engineer — 让 AI 承担 heavy lifting。
Full-stack skill 加 business judgment — 通过 orchestrating agents 实现

这是这个角色的核心。在 CHI，“operator” 意味着 orchestrating agents，而不是手动做所有事。我们期待你已经：
• 每天用 AI coding agents ship production code — 这是默认工作方式，不是小把戏
• 设计并运行 multi-agent workflows：review、QA、deployment watching、incident drafting，并从每次运行中改进
• 用 AI debug incidents：喂给它 logs、configs、stack traces，并推动到 root cause
• 围绕 AI 构建 automation，而不只是用 AI — agents、review bots、report generators、internal tools
• 知道 AI 会在哪里错：你 verify、test，并 own output。Agent speed with human judgment.
• 边做边写 documentation 和 runbooks，因为生成它们只需要几分钟

你的工作不是手动覆盖一个 vertical — 而是 design、ship 和 manage 运行它的 agent workforce，并在只有人类判断能解决的地方介入。
我们期待
• 强 backend skills（TypeScript / Node.js 或 equivalent — 愿意深入我们的 stack）
• 真正的 DevOps：Docker、Linux、networking、CI/CD、logs、monitoring — 以及凌晨 1 点 debug prod 的经验
• Product sense：你能把 feature 从 spec 带到 shipped UI 和 API，并在意 organizers 和 attendees 的实际体验
• 扎实理解 APIs、databases、queues、authentication 和 distributed systems
• Ownership：看到问题，fix it、automate it、document it — 进入 shared knowledge base 和 agents 的 self-learning loops
• Business judgment：operators own product、ops 和 finance 的 outcomes — 不只是 code
• 清晰的书面英语 — 大多数协调都是 async 和 written
• 重视 stability 和 security：我们处理 payments；粗心代价很高
加分项
• 票务 / POS / 活动科技
• Stripe Connect / 交易市场
• PCI DSS / 安全加固
• RBAC / Vault 密钥
• Android POS / 移动端
• 构建过 AI agents / dev tooling
• 快速发展的初创公司
普通团队给不了的 leverage
• 真实 stakes: Live events、live payments、live vendors。你的工作在 crowds 面前运行，而不是在 sprint backlog 里。
• Agents，而不是 seats: Few humans，每个人都有一支 agents workforce。你的 leverage 是普通团队的倍数。
• 完整 ownership: 没有 ticket-shuffling，没有三层 approval。同一周里做 product、backend、infra 和 AI tooling。
• 自主化公司的前沿: 大多数公司只是在写 AI-native teams 的文章。我们就是其中一个 — 你将帮助定义它如何运作。
• 利益绑定: Base 之上的 revenue share — platform earns 时，你也 earn。每个人的 upside 都应该如此。
• 巴厘岛 base，远程职能: 我们保留 Indonesia/Bali office base 用于实时协作，也支持远程工作，前提是时区重叠、ownership 和客户责任保持强。
• 活动现场访问: 我们的 platform runs festivals。你会在现场看到自己的工作。
• 工具预算: 我们支付让你更快的 AI tools 和 hardware — 包括 local-inference rigs 以及 frontier APIs。
如何申请

Email work@chi.app with:
• 你的 CV 或 LinkedIn
• GitHub 或你的作品示例
• 一段简短说明：你如何在日常 workflow 中使用 AI — 具体写明哪些 tools、用途，以及你用它们 built 或 automated 的一件事
• 一个你 end to end own 的 infrastructure、automation 或 DevOps 工作示例

我们会先读 AI-workflow note。优秀的 note 会在几天内收到回复 — “我用 ChatGPT 写邮件” 不算。

• Own systems outright. One or two products are yours: API contracts, data models, service boundaries, performance. You make the architectural calls and defend them in review.

• You build it, you run it. Deploy, monitor, fix. Nobody hands your service off to an ops team.

• Mentor our junior engineers. Two of them, hungry and improving fast. Code review and pairing are part of the job, not something you squeeze in.

Our Stack & What We Need

Kotlin is the core of this role, not an item on a list — you'll be writing, reviewing, and shipping it from week one.

• Kotlin: 2+ years of production experience required. A Java/JVM background only counts if you've already shipped real Kotlin — this isn't a "pick it up here" role.

• Spring Boot & PostgreSQL: our core backend stack, day-to-day.

• React & GraphQL: used on the frontend side — comfort ramping up is fine if it's not already your daily driver.

• AWS: a bonus, not a requirement.

Beyond the stack, we're looking for:

• Real production experience — you've designed schemas that outlived their first assumptions, debugged something ugly at scale, and have opinions about monitoring.

• Self-direction. You ask good questions, then go.

supply chain, logistics, or accounting domain experience microservices at scale prior work shipping LLM-powered or agentic features open source.

• A CTO whose job is unblocking you and helping you grow

Company OverviewVascomm is a technology company committed to delivering BRIGHT solutions for business. We have established strategic partnerships with leading telecommunication companies and banks to design and develop branchless banking platforms, server-based e-money systems, and internal enterprise information systems. Our solutions empower various business sectors to scale and expand their market reach across cities throughout Indonesia.Role OverviewThe development of reliable applications and systems must be supported by a robust and secure infrastructure, with database infrastructure being a critical component. As a Database Engineer, you will be responsible for managing database systems from an infrastructure and security perspective. This role involves supporting the installation, configuration, optimization, and deployment of database servers to ensure system reliability, performance, and data integrity.Responsibilities

• Installation, configuration, and maintenance of MySQL/Percona/MariaDB databases.
• Database performance monitoring (CPU, memory, disk, IOPS, connections, query latency).

• Implementation and maintenance of replication/high availability (Master-Slave, Galera/PXC).
• Layer 2/Layer 3 database incident handling (performance drops, replication lag, corruption).
• Database security implementation: user and privilege management, audit logs, secure access.
• Support for Disaster Recovery Plan (DRP) and information security audit requirements.
• Documentation of SOPs, runbooks, and regular database health reports.
• Collaboration with Developers, SysOps, DevOps, and IT Security regarding application requirements.

Requirement

• Bachelor’s degree (S1/D3) in Computer Science, Information Systems, or equivalent.
• 3–4 years of hands-on experience managing MySQL databases in production environments.
• Strong knowledge of MySQL (InnoDB, indexing, transactions, locking).
• Experience with database backup, restore, performance tuning, and troubleshooting.
• Proficient in Linux command line (Red Hat–based).
• Experience with monitoring tools (Prometheus, Grafana, Zabbix, or equivalent).
• Basic understanding of networking and system security.
• Familiar with automation (Shell Script/Ansible) and cloud databases (AWS RDS or Cloud SQL) is a plus.
• Strong problem-solving skills, attention to detail, ownership mindset, and effective cross-team communication.

Pengambilan Sampel (Sampling): Melaksanakan proses pengambilan sampel material secara akurat sesuai dengan titik pengecekan yang diatur dalam Quality Plan dan Instruksi Kerja (IK) inspeksi. Inspeksi & Pengukuran Kualitas: Melakukan pengujian dimensi dan inspeksi visual pada sampel material secara presisi berdasarkan standar AQL ( Acceptance Quality Level ) dan kriteria mutu perusahaan. Penyusunan Laporan: Membuat dan menyusun laporan hasil inspeksi secara berkala dan akurat, baik untuk material dengan status PASS (diterima) maupun REJECT (ditolak). Distribusi Informasi: Mengirimkan laporan hasil inspeksi secara berkala kepada seluruh pihak internal yang terkait melalui email secara tepat waktu. Penanganan Material Non-Conformance: Menerbitkan Non-Conformance Report (NCR) jika ditemukan material yang REJECT , serta berkoordinasi aktif dengan Admin & Supervisor Warehouse mengenai status dan penanganan material bermasalah tersebut. Keahlian Teknis QA/QC: Menguasai teknik sampling, metode pengukuran material (dimensi & visual), serta pemahaman standar AQL. Sistem & Administrasi: Menguasai penggunaan NC Catalog , sistem ERP (INFOR/sejenis), Ms. Excel (untuk pengolahan data laporan), dan korespondensi Email profesional. Pengetahuan Produk & Proses: Memahami spesifikasi packaging material serta memiliki pengetahuan dasar tentang proses cutting kertas cones & filter . Alur Kerja & Regulasi: Memahami workflow penerimaan barang di Warehouse serta memiliki pemahaman dasar ( awareness ) terkait Sistem Manajemen Mutu (ISO 9001:2015). Kompetensi Perilaku: Memiliki tingkat ketelitian yang tinggi ( attention to detail ), kemampuan komunikasi/koordinasi yang baik, dan integritas dalam menjaga standar kualitas.

About the role

Majura AI is a pre-seed startup building the operating system and agentic AI layer for Indonesia's logistics ecosystem, founded by Silicon Valley transplants — CTO (ex-Airbnb, YComb) and CEO (ex-TikTok, Lyft). This is our first senior engineering hire, reporting directly to the CTO, to own architecture across our product surface as we scale into Q4.

Location

Surabaya, Hybrid (3 days/week in office) — remote considered for eligible candidates

Salary

Rp.15 – 45 juta /month, based on experience and interview performance

Reports to

CTO

What You'll Do

• Work autonomously. Sometimes you'll get a spec. Sometimes you'll get a problem and a customer, and you figure out the rest. Big calls get a quick sign-off from the CTO — everything else is yours. No ticket queue, no committee, no waiting weeks for a decision.

• Own systems outright. One or two products are yours: API contracts, data models, service boundaries, performance. You make the architectural calls and defend them in review.

• Build our AI infrastructure from the ground up. We're early here — the foundations aren't built yet. Help us build them and they're yours to own and grow with as the company scales.

• You build it, you run it. Deploy, monitor, fix. Nobody hands your service off to an ops team.

• Mentor our junior engineers. Two of them, hungry and improving fast. Code review and pairing are part of the job, not something you squeeze in.

Our Stack & What We Need

Kotlin is the core of this role, not an item on a list — you'll be writing, reviewing, and shipping it from week one.

• Kotlin: 2+ years of production experience required. A Java/JVM background only counts if you've already shipped real Kotlin — this isn't a "pick it up here" role.

• Spring Boot & PostgreSQL: our core backend stack, day-to-day.

• React & GraphQL: used on the frontend side — comfort ramping up is fine if it's not already your daily driver.

• AWS: a bonus, not a requirement.

Beyond the stack, we're looking for:

• Real production experience — you've designed schemas that outlived their first assumptions, debugged something ugly at scale, and have opinions about monitoring.

• Self-direction. You ask good questions, then go.

• Writing. Design docs, API documentation, clear PR descriptions. We're small and moving fast; writing is how we stay coordinated.

• Comfort with ambiguity. You'll make decisions on incomplete information and occasionally be wrong. Some of what you build in year one will get rewritten.

• Fluent in English. Speak, read, write clearly at a professional proficiency or better

Bonus:

supply chain, logistics, or accounting domain experience microservices at scale prior work shipping LLM-powered or agentic features open source.

About us

Majura is building Agentic AI and SaaS products for Indonesia's $150B+ logistics ecosystem — not generic SaaS, but infrastructure with immediate, real-world impact. Visit us at https://majura.ai/

Compensation & Benefits

• Salary range: Rp.15 – 45 juta per month (based on experience & interview)

• Profit sharing (our version of equity)

• Performance bonus structure based on milestones

• Learning budget for conferences, courses, and tools

• Hybrid: 3 days in our Surabaya office, flexible on the rest

• A CTO whose job is unblocking you and helping you grow

Interview Process

• 30-minute screening call on WhatsApp

• 45-minute coding interview with the CTO

• 1-hour interview with the team

About Mobbin

Our mission is to empower the world to design great digital experiences.

Mobbin helps designers and product people find highly-relevant references to their design problems. Today, Mobbin is serving over 3 million users and is used by most design-forward companies such as Wise, Airbnb, Headspace, Duolingo, Uber, and more.

Contract (Full-time), Remote

Note that this is not a UX Designer, UX Researcher, or UX Writer role. You will not be designing or conducting research in any capacity. Instead, you will spend most of your time dissecting apps and taking screenshots.
The role

At Mobbin, we curate thousands of app screenshots every week. Our team of analysts meticulously organizes and tags them by hand, ensuring that our users have access to the most comprehensive references.

As a Content Analyst, you will play a crucial role in ensuring that our library is constantly updated with fresh content for our users.

Each week, you will analyze the best-in-class apps and conduct a detailed breakdown. Your analysis will provide valuable insights to our users, who use it as direct input for their design decisions.
What you’ll do...
• Acquire and prepare content on a weekly basis, following our guidelines.
• Conduct a detailed analysis and breakdown of mobile apps.
• Curate screens and flows following our guidelines on design patterns and UI elements.
• Collaborate with other team members to ensure that all content meets our quality standards.

At Agoda, we bridge the world through travel. Our story began in 2005, when two lifelong friends and entrepreneurs, driven by their passion for travel, launched Agoda to make it easier for everyone to explore the world.

At Agoda, our Backend Engineering team builds high-scale, fault-tolerant distributed systems that power a global travel platform serving millions of users daily. We own mission-critical domains across inventory, pricing, booking, payments, and customer/partner platforms. About Mobbin

Our mission is to empower the world to design great digital experiences.

Mobbin helps designers and product people find highly-relevant references to their design problems. Today, Mobbin is serving over 3 million users and is used by most design-forward companies such as Wise, Airbnb, Headspace, Duolingo, Uber, and more.

Read more about who we are:

Contract (Full-time), Remote

The role

At Mobbin, we curate thousands of app screenshots every week. Our team of analysts meticulously organizes and tags them by hand, ensuring that our users have access to the most comprehensive references.

As a Content Analyst, you will play a crucial role in ensuring that our library is constantly updated with fresh content for our users.

About the role The Spatial Data Analyst is responsible for building, processing, analyzing, and validating geospatial datasets to support the development of the AI Disaster Mitigation Platform, particularly for weather monitoring and earthquake-induced ground deformation mapping. This role focuses on transforming satellite observations and geospatial datasets into reliable disaster information through remote sensing, geospatial analysis, and automated data processing workflows. The analyst will work with Himawari-8/9 or relevant weather satellite data for near real-time weather visualization and Sentinel-1 SAR data for automated ground deformation analysis related to earthquakes.

Key responsibilities

• Build and maintain automated pipelines that ingest and process Himawari-8/9 data in near real time (calibration, band composites, cloud and rainfall-related products, tiling-ready outputs)

• Evaluate and implement methods to handle Himawari's coarse pixel size, such as resampling/interpolation, band sharpening, and downscaling, and document the trade-offs with evidence

• Develop automated Sentinel-1 SAR / InSAR workflows to map earthquake-induced ground deformation, including image pair selection, interferogram processing, unwrapping, geocoding, and LOS displacement products

• Design event-triggered automation (e.g., earthquake catalogue feeds to satellite data search and processing) using Python and workflow orchestration tools

• Use Sentinel-2, ALOS, and other satellite data to support disaster mapping (flood, landslide, and typhoon-related analysis) as required

• Prepare and manage spatial datasets (COG, GeoTIFF, NetCDF, PostGIS) for dashboard visualization

• Collaborate with the Fullstack Website Developer to integrate spatial outputs (tiles, APIs, metadata) into the web platform

• Produce maps, visualizations, technical documentation, methodology, and analysis reports

Requirements

• Bachelor's degree in Geodetic Engineering, Geography, Geomatics, Remote Sensing, Geophysics, Meteorology, Environmental Science, or a related field

• Experienced in remote sensing or spatial data analysis (final year student or fresh graduates with relevant thesis or project experience are welcome to apply)

• Hands-on experience with weather / geostationary satellite data, preferably Himawari-8/9 (AHI) or similar and its data formats, calibration, band combinations, and cloud/rain interpretation

• Strong Python skills for geospatial automation (e.g., GDAL/rasterio, xarray, NumPy, geopandas, satpy)

• Experience processing Sentinel data (Sentinel-1 and/or Sentinel-2) using SNAP, Google Earth Engine, or Python, solid understanding of SAR fundamentals

• Understanding of disaster and hazard analysis, especially earthquakes, floods, landslides, and typhoons, and how satellite data support them

• Familiarity with geospatial data management (PostgreSQL/PostGIS, Cloud Optimized GeoTIFF, STAC)

• Good technical writing and communication in English; ability to work independently and in a cross-functional team

Additional Information

• Work Location: HQuarters Business Residence, Jl. Asia Afrika No.158 UNIT 10-Q, Paledang, Kec. Lengkong, Kota Bandung, Jawa Barat.

• Work Arrangement: Hybrid (Work from Office & Work from Home)

raw.job_description:
AI Application Engineer (LLM, RAG & Agentic Systems)

As an AI Application Engineer, you will build the AI layer of our products: retrieval systems, LLM orchestration, and the evaluation harness that keeps them reliable in production. You will work in a two-person engineering pair with our web developer, who owns the application, while you own the AI service behind it.

The role has a clear trajectory. You will start with retrieval and single-turn generation, where correctness is measurable and the ground is solid. As the product matures, you will extend the same system into multi-step agentic workflows: tool use, planning, background execution, and human-in-the-loop approval. We move in that order deliberately. An agent built on unevaluated retrieval fails in ways nobody can debug.

This is an applied engineering role. You will not train models from scratch. You will make foundation models work correctly, cheaply, and predictably on real data.

Our working language is English. You will collaborate with colleagues in Singapore and with international partners, and you will read documentation, model provider guidance, and research that exists only in English.
Key responsibilities
• Design and build retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) pipelines end to end: document ingestion, chunking, embedding, hybrid search, and reranking
• Develop and maintain the LLM orchestration layer, including prompt and context assembly, structured output, and tool or function calling
• Build and own an evaluation harness: golden datasets, regression testing on every prompt or model change, and failure analysis. Extend it to trajectory-level evaluation as workflows become multi-step
• Design and implement agentic capabilities as the product requires them: tool definitions and schemas, multi-step planning, state and memory across turns, retry and fallback behaviour, and human approval checkpoints for consequential actions
• Instrument and control token cost, latency, and model routing, escalating from cheap to premium models only where quality requires it. Enforce step and spend ceilings on any autonomous loop
• Expose the AI layer as a documented, versioned API consumed by the web application, with clear contracts and error handling
• Implement guardrails against prompt injection, data leakage, and unsafe tool use, and enforce data boundaries for client information. No unattended writes to production systems without an approval gate
• Document architecture decisions and share knowledge across the engineering team
About you
• Professional working proficiency in English, written and spoken
• 2+ years building production software, with at least 1 year shipping LLM-based applications to real users
• Strong Python, including a production web framework such as FastAPI
• Direct experience with LLM provider APIs (Anthropic, OpenAI, or Google) at the API level, not only through high-level wrappers
• Demonstrated RAG experience built from components: chunking strategy, embedding models, a vector store (pgvector, Qdrant, Weaviate, or similar), BM25 or hybrid search, and reranking
• Practical experience with tool and function calling, structured output, and schema enforcement
• Practical experience evaluating LLM systems: building test sets, measuring quality, and preventing regressions
• Working knowledge of PostgreSQL, Git, Docker, and CI/CD
• Comfortable owning cost and latency budgets, and reasoning about tradeoffs between quality, speed, and spend
• Excellent problem-solving skills, with the ability to work independently in a small team
About us

SL2 Group (sustainablelivinglab.org) is an ecosystem of organizations that design and implement solutions to navigate climate, societal, and digital transitions. Founded in Singapore in 2011, we work globally with governments, companies, and grassroots to address issues from climate adaptation and circular economies to green and tech upskilling and community inclusion. By uniting foresight, technology, and community engagement, our collective transforms ideas into scalable impact.

The ideal candidate is comfortable working in environments where test automation practices are evolving, and can contribute effectively during testing framework transitions while maintaining quality standards.

Saatnya upgrade peranmu bareng tim SEVIMA sebagai Software QA Engineer! Let’s build impact.

Sebagai Software QA Engineer Peranmu Adalah..

• Meninjau kebutuhan, spesifikasi, dan dokumen desain teknis untuk memberikan masukan yang tepat.

• Terus mengikuti perkembangan terbaru terkait tools dan strategi testing.

ROLE OVERVIEW

We are looking for a full-time Quality Assurance (QA) Automation Engineer who is passionate about delivering high-quality software products. This is a fully remote position, allowing you to contribute from anywhere while collaborating closely with our dynamic, distributed team. You will be responsible for ensuring the reliability, functionality, and usability of our web-based applications.

You will work on a large-scale supply chain management system that supports core business operations, including demand–supply planning and warehouse processes. The platform is actively evolving and operates in a production environment, requiring strong automation practices to maintain stability while enabling safe and continuous improvements.

This role is heavily focused on web automation using Playwright, with manual testing performed when necessary. You will collaborate closely with developers and product teams to implement shift-left testing, ensure early validation, and support high-velocity Agile releases.

The ideal candidate is comfortable working in environments where test automation practices are evolving, and can contribute effectively during testing framework transitions while maintaining quality standards.

This position is well suited for mid-to-senior QA Automation Engineers who enjoy building and refining automation frameworks, working with real-world production systems, and taking ownership of quality in complex applications.

REQUIREMENTS

• Bachelor’s degree (S1) in Computer Science, Information Technology, or a related field.

• Clear communication skills in English, both written and verbal.

JOB DESCRIPTION

• Design, develop, and maintain automated test cases using Playwright.

• Collaborate with development and product teams during planning and design phases to support testability and early validation.

• Conduct exploratory testing to uncover usability issues and edge cases.

• Apply risk-based prioritization to focus automation efforts on critical user flows.

• Identify, log, and clearly communicate defects, including their technical and business impact.

• Perform regression, functional, UI, performance, and basic security testing as needed.

• Support post-release and post-deployment testing in production-like environments.

• Contribute to continuous improvement of QA processes, documentation, and automation strategy.

NICE TO HAVE

• Experience integrating automation tests into CI/CD pipelines (GitLab CI, Jenkins).

About the project (description, duration, stage)

Join Neurons Lab as a Data Engineer (part-time) on a flagship engagement with a European private investment group — a holding company with a C-level executive team, an investment/portfolio function and an affiliated family office.

The programme builds one private, access-scoped context layer over the group's data, then AI skills and agents on top of it. You build the plumbing underneath: Phase 1 (Capture) — turn on ingestion across calls, email, Slack and messengers, board protocols, decks and portfolio updates, live and historical; Phase 2 (Connect) — land it all in the context layer with identity resolved, access scope attached and lineage intact.

This is deliberately an unstructured-first data-engineering role. There is no clean warehouse to model: the raw material is transcripts, threads, attachments and years of archive, and the hard problems are entity resolution across people and entities, deduplication, incremental sync, PII handling, and keeping cost sane at volume.

Roughly eight to ten two-week sprints overall, with your load front-weighted to the first four or five — allocation may flex above 0.5 FTE during Capture and Connect and settle back afterwards.

Stage: active project, start ASAP.

Part-time, 20 to 30 hours-a-week engagement.

What you'll actually do (example tasks)

• Stand up capture by default: notetaker on every call with speaker attribution, plus ingestion from mail, Slack and messengers — designed as opt-out, not opt-in, and reversible if the client changes their mind.

• Backfill the archive: years of historical email, Slack, board protocols, decks and portfolio updates — parsed, deduplicated and dated correctly.

• Build document parsing for the awkward long tail: PDFs, scanned board packs, spreadsheets, slide decks, forwarded attachments.

• Implement identity / entity resolution: the same person across Slack handle, mail alias and calendar invite; the same portfolio company across a deck, a mail thread and a CRM record.

• Build chunking and embedding pipelines and load the vector + graph stores behind the ontology the architect defines.

• Implement incremental sync through the connector layer (MCP / Composio-class) — no full re-crawls, no silent drift, clear handling of edits and deletions.

• Attach access scope and provenance to every record at ingestion, so permission-aware retrieval and audit are possible downstream rather than bolted on.

• Run PII detection, redaction and retention logic; evidence to the client's security function what is stored, where, and for how long.

• Orchestrate with Airflow / Step Functions; build repeatable, monitored pipelines rather than scripts, with alerting when a source stops flowing.

• Keep cost and latency under control at volume — batching, incremental embedding, storage tiering — and report the unit economics.

• Write runbooks so the client's own team can operate this after handover.

Skills

• Strong Python and solid SQL

• Unstructured-data pipelines: transcripts, mail, chat, documents — parsing, normalisation, deduplication

• Embedding / retrieval infrastructure: chunking strategies, vector stores (pgvector, OpenSearch, Pinecone-class), plus loading a graph store

• API and connector integration at scale: Google Workspace / M365, Slack, CRM; rate limits, pagination, incremental cursors, webhooks

• Entity resolution / record linkage (deterministic + fuzzy) without a clean shared key

• Orchestration: Airflow, Step Functions or equivalent; idempotent, restartable jobs

• AWS and/or GCP data stack; comfortable in a private / VPC deployment

• PII detection, redaction, encryption and retention in practice

• Clear written English; documents for handover and works well async in a small distributed pod

Knowledge

• GDPR applied to employee-generated data (mail, chat, meeting recordings) and EU data residency across multiple jurisdictions

• Data lineage, provenance and audit patterns — and why an AI system needs them more, not less

• How retrieval quality depends on ingestion quality — enough understanding of RAG to make the right upstream choices

• Well-Architected security and cost practice; awareness of financial-services expectations — a plus

Experience

• 4+ years in data engineering, with real unstructured / semi-structured work (not only warehouse modelling)

• Demonstrated experience integrating many third-party APIs into one coherent store, including historical backfill

• Experience building pipelines feeding an LLM / retrieval system — strong plus

• Experience handling sensitive personal data in a regulated or security-sensitive environment

• Comfortable being the only data engineer on a small (2.5-FTE) pod, at part-time allocation, without hand-holding

About the project (description, duration, stage)

Join Neurons Lab as a Data Engineer (part-time) on a flagship engagement with a European private investment group — a holding company with a C-level executive team, an investment/portfolio function and an affiliated family office.

The programme builds one private, access-scoped context layer over the group's data, then AI skills and agents on top of it. You build the plumbing underneath: Phase 1 (Capture) — turn on ingestion across calls, email, Slack and messengers, board protocols, decks and portfolio updates, live and historical; Phase 2 (Connect) — land it all in the context layer with identity resolved, access scope attached and lineage intact.

This is deliberately an unstructured-first data-engineering role. There is no clean warehouse to model: the raw material is transcripts, threads, attachments and years of archive, and the hard problems are entity resolution across people and entities, deduplication, incremental sync, PII handling, and keeping cost sane at volume.

Roughly eight to ten two-week sprints overall, with your load front-weighted to the first four or five — allocation may flex above 0.5 FTE during Capture and Connect and settle back afterwards.

Part-time, 20 to 30 hours-a-week engagement.

What you'll actually do (example tasks)

• Stand up capture by default: notetaker on every call with speaker attribution, plus ingestion from mail, Slack and messengers — designed as opt-out, not opt-in, and reversible if the client changes their mind.

• Backfill the archive: years of historical email, Slack, board protocols, decks and portfolio updates — parsed, deduplicated and dated correctly.

• Build document parsing for the awkward long tail: PDFs, scanned board packs, spreadsheets, slide decks, forwarded attachments.

• Implement identity / entity resolution: the same person across Slack handle, mail alias and calendar invite; the same portfolio company across a deck, a mail thread and a CRM record.

• Build chunking and embedding pipelines and load the vector + graph stores behind the ontology the architect defines.

• Implement incremental sync through the connector layer (MCP / Composio-class) — no full re-crawls, no silent drift, clear handling of edits and deletions.

• Attach access scope and provenance to every record at ingestion, so permission-aware retrieval and audit are possible downstream rather than bolted on.

• Run PII detection, redaction and retention logic; evidence to the client's security function what is stored, where, and for how long.

• Orchestrate with Airflow / Step Functions; build repeatable, monitored pipelines rather than scripts, with alerting when a source stops flowing.

• Keep cost and latency under control at volume — batching, incremental embedding, storage tiering — and report the unit economics.

• Write runbooks so the client's own team can operate this after handover.

Skills

• Strong Python and solid SQL

• Unstructured-data pipelines: transcripts, mail, chat, documents — parsing, normalisation, deduplication

• Embedding / retrieval infrastructure: chunking strategies, vector stores (pgvector, OpenSearch, Pinecone-class), plus loading a graph store

• API and connector integration at scale: Google Workspace / M365, Slack, CRM; rate limits, pagination, incremental cursors, webhooks

• Entity resolution / record linkage (deterministic + fuzzy) without a clean shared key

• Orchestration: Airflow, Step Functions or equivalent; idempotent, restartable jobs

• AWS and/or GCP data stack; comfortable in a private / VPC deployment

• PII detection, redaction, encryption and retention in practice

• Clear written English; documents for handover and works well async in a small distributed pod

Knowledge

raw.job_description:
About the Role

VIDA verifies identity in real time for financial services, lending, telecommunications, and government-linked services. This makes us a target for organised fraud operations that spoof genuine users and devices at scale — and adapt within days when a defence starts working. Detection here is a continuing contest, and errors cost in both directions: missed fraud harms users and customers, while false positives deny real people access to services.

You will own detection on this path: investigate attacks in raw device and behavioural telemetry, build the rules and ML models that catch them, and measure what they catch and what they cost genuine users. The data is high-dimensional and noisy, labels are scarce and delayed, and decisions must be explainable.

What You Will Do

Understand the adversary
• Investigate real attacks — reconstruct how a campaign operates from the evidence available, and characterise it well enough that we can act on it.
• Find signal in high-dimensional, messy data — work across large volumes of device and behavioural telemetry to identify what genuinely separates fraudulent activity from legitimate users.
• Keep pace with change — when an adversary adapts, quickly establish what changed and what still distinguishes them.

Build detection that holds up
• Design detection logic and models — from feature engineering through training, calibration, and threshold selection, choosing the right tool for the problem: interpretable logic where explainability matters, models where they earn their place.
• Detect coordinated activity, not just single events — move detection beyond judging each request in isolation toward recognising organised behaviour across many, which is far harder for an adversary to disguise.
• Balance detection against user impact — treat the false-positive cost to genuine users as a first-class constraint, measured on the real population before anything is enforced.
• Own quality in production — validate before enforcement, monitor for drift and degradation, and know when to roll back.

Make the evidence trustworthy
• Build and improve ground truth — establish reliable labels in a domain where they are scarce, delayed, and imperfect, and be clear about what your labels do and do not cover.
• Hold a high evidential bar — recall and false-positive rates measured on the right populations, class imbalance, selection bias, and correctness of point-in-time evaluation. You should be able to spot the ways an analysis can flatter itself, and design around them.
• Make the work reproducible and legible — analysis and specifications that colleagues can re-run, challenge, and build on.
• Partner closely with fraud operations, engineering, and product — and communicate findings clearly to non-specialists, including when the honest answer is uncomfortable.

What We Are Looking For

Must-have
• 4+ years of applied data science or machine learning in fraud, risk, abuse, trust & safety, security, or a closely adjacent adversarial domain — with work you took to production and measured.
• Strong SQL on large datasets — comfortable and effective in large, messy event data.
• Fluent Python data-science stack — pandas, scikit-learn, and gradient-boosted trees, with clean and reproducible analysis.
• Genuine evaluation rigour — you understand why a model can look excellent offline and fail in production: label leakage, selection bias, drift, class imbalance, and the difference between conditioned and population-level error rates.
• Feature engineering from raw, semi-structured data — turning noisy, high-cardinality inputs into signals that hold up over time.
• An adversarial mindset — you instinctively ask how someone would evade what you built, and you design accordingly.
• Sound judgement on explainability — decisions affecting a person's access to services need to be defensible, not just accurate.
• Ownership and pragmatism — you can carry a problem from ambiguous question to shipped, measured outcome without waiting to be handed a specification.

Nice-to-have
• Device intelligence, device fingerprinting, or bot and automated-abuse detection.
• Biometrics, liveness, or presentation- and injection-attack detection.
• Mobile platform knowledge, including device integrity and attestation concepts.
• Graph analysis or entity resolution for linking related activity and identifying organised rings.
• Real-time or streaming features and the discipline of keeping training and serving consistent.
• Experience in emerging markets or high-growth financial services.
• Comfort using AI-assisted tooling to work faster without lowering the evidential bar.

What are we trying to solve?

We have 7.5 billion people on Earth, of which over 1 billion cannot securely prove their identity right now. Every year, 140 million babies are born, of which 40 million go unregistered. Simply put, these people are deprived of social benefits, such as education and health, their civil rights to vote and travel; and are excluded from the economy because they cannot sign up for bank accounts, loans, welfare programs etc. We believe this is unacceptable, and needs to change.

At VIDA, we are creating a frictionless digital identity system. One that fulfils the needs and expectations of our times, and is available anywhere, for everyone.

Why are we solving this problem?

The United Nations (UN) and World Bank ID4D initiatives aim to provide everyone on the planet with a legal identity by 2030. This deadline is just a few years away, we are expecting a digital identity to be a legal human right by then and we at VIDA want to be pioneers in leading this change.

Who are we?

We are a highly driven bunch of people solving this problem for our own reasons. Whether it is misleading doctors, or because we didn't get access to fair ration due to corruption — our collective goal aligns.

• Build document parsing for the awkward long tail: PDFs, scanned board packs, spreadsheets, slide decks, forwarded attachments.

• Implement identity / entity resolution: the same person across Slack handle, mail alias and calendar invite; the same portfolio company across a deck, a mail thread and a CRM record.

• Build chunking and embedding pipelines and load the vector + graph stores behind the ontology the architect defines.

• Implement incremental sync through the connector layer (MCP / Composio-class) — no full re-crawls, no silent drift, clear handling of edits and deletions.

• Orchestrate with Airflow / Step Functions; build repeatable, monitored pipelines rather than scripts, with alerting when a source stops flowing.

raw.job_description:
VIDA verifies identity in real time for financial services, lending, telecommunications, and government-linked services. This makes us a target for organised fraud operations that spoof genuine users and devices at scale — and adapt within days when a defence starts working. Detection here is a continuing contest, and errors cost in both directions: missed fraud harms users and customers, while false positives deny real people access to services.

You will own detection on this path: investigate attacks in raw device and behavioural telemetry, build the rules and ML models that catch them, and measure what they catch and what they cost genuine users. The data is high-dimensional and noisy, labels are scarce and delayed, and decisions must be explainable.
What You Will Do
Understand the adversary
• Investigate real attacks — reconstruct how a campaign operates from the evidence available, and characterise it well enough that we can act on it.
• Find signal in high-dimensional, messy data — work across large volumes of device and behavioural telemetry to identify what genuinely separates fraudulent activity from legitimate users.
• Keep pace with change — when an adversary adapts, quickly establish what changed and what still distinguishes them.
Build detection that holds up
• Design detection logic and models — from feature engineering through training, calibration, and threshold selection, choosing the right tool for the problem: interpretable logic where explainability matters, models where they earn their place.
• Detect coordinated activity, not just single events — move detection beyond judging each request in isolation toward recognising organised behaviour across many, which is far harder for an adversary to disguise.
• Balance detection against user impact — treat the false-positive cost to genuine users as a first-class constraint, measured on the real population before anything is enforced.
• Own quality in production — validate before enforcement, monitor for drift and degradation, and know when to roll back.
Make the evidence trustworthy
• Build and improve ground truth — establish reliable labels in a domain where they are scarce, delayed, and imperfect, and be clear about what your labels do and do not cover.
• Hold a high evidential bar — recall and false-positive rates measured on the right populations, class imbalance, selection bias, and correctness of point-in-time evaluation. You should be able to spot the ways an analysis can flatter itself, and design around them.
• Make the work reproducible and legible — analysis and specifications that colleagues can re-run, challenge, and build on.
• Partner closely with fraud operations, engineering, and product — and communicate findings clearly to non-specialists, including when the honest answer is uncomfortable.
What We Are Looking For
Must-have
• 4+ years of applied data science or machine learning in fraud, risk, abuse, trust & safety, security, or a closely adjacent adversarial domain — with work you took to production and measured.
• Strong SQL on large datasets — comfortable and effective in large, messy event data.
• Fluent Python data-science stack — pandas, scikit-learn, and gradient-boosted trees, with clean and reproducible analysis.
• Genuine evaluation rigour — you understand why a model can look excellent offline and fail in production: label leakage, selection bias, drift, class imbalance, and the difference between conditioned and population-level error rates.
• Feature engineering from raw, semi-structured data — turning noisy, high-cardinality inputs into signals that hold up over time.
• An adversarial mindset — you instinctively ask how someone would evade what you built, and you design accordingly.
• Sound judgement on explainability — decisions affecting a person's access to services need to be defensible, not just accurate.
• Ownership and pragmatism — you can carry a problem from ambiguous question to shipped, measured outcome without waiting to be handed a specification.
Nice-to-have
• Device intelligence, device fingerprinting, or bot and automated-abuse detection.
• Biometrics, liveness, or presentation- and injection-attack detection.
• Mobile platform knowledge, including device integrity and attestation concepts.
• Graph analysis or entity resolution for linking related activity and identifying organised rings.
• Real-time or streaming features and the discipline of keeping training and serving consistent.
• Experience in emerging markets or high-growth financial services.
• Comfort using AI-assisted tooling to work faster without lowering the evidential bar.
What are we trying to solve?

We have 7.5 billion people on Earth, of which over 1 billion cannot securely prove their identity right now. Every year, 140 million babies are born, of which 40 million go unregistered. Simply put, these people are deprived of social benefits, such as education and health, their civil rights to vote and travel; and are excluded from the economy because they cannot sign up for bank accounts, loans, welfare programs etc. We believe this is unacceptable, and needs to change.

At VIDA, we are creating a frictionless digital identity system. One that fulfils the needs and expectations of our times, and is available anywhere, for everyone.
Why are we solving this problem?

The United Nations (UN) and World Bank ID4D initiatives aim to provide everyone on the planet with a legal identity by 2030. This deadline is just a few years away, we are expecting a digital identity to be a legal human right by then and we at VIDA want to be pioneers in leading this change.
Who are we?

We are a highly driven bunch of people solving this problem for our own reasons. Whether it is misleading doctors, or because we didn't get access to fair ration due to corruption — our collective goal aligns.

Do you want to become an ambassador for a globally recognized high quality brand?

Are you ready for the new challenges?

Join our organization and help us build the best in class global IT function that is technologically sound, future proof and can react quickly to ever-changing demands!

Some career choices have more impact than others. When you join ECCO, you become part of a global family where we value people who do things differently. BE DIFFERENT AND FIT IN!

Job Purpose

As a Senior Frontend Engineer within our eCommerce team, you will help shape the future of our digital shopping experience. In this high-impact role, you will build performant, scalable, and user-friendly interfaces using Next.js, React, and modern web technologies. Your work will directly influence customer engagement and conversion across our global online platforms.

Responsibilities

• Optimize performance, accessibility, and SEO across all pages and components.

• Collaborate closely with product owners, designers, and backend engineers to deliver seamless user experiences.

• Stay up to date with the latest frontend technologies and advocate for best practices.

• Architect reusable components and scalable frontend systems

• Implement and maintain CI/CD pipelines and frontend testing strategies.

• Lead the development of new features and enhancements using Next.js, React, and TypeScript.

• Mentor junior developers and contribute to code reviews and technical discussions.

Requirements

• 5+ years of front-end development experience with a strong focus on React and Next.js.

• Deep understanding of TypeScript, modern JavaScript and browser fundamentals.

• Experience building and maintaining large-scale web applications, in high-traffic e-commerce environments.

• Solid understanding of SSR, SSG, ISR, and edge rendering strategies, including trade-offs between performance, cost, and complexity.

• Experience working with headless CMS, search platforms and API-driven architectures (GraphQL/REST).

• Strong focus on web performance (Core Web Vitals), accessibility (WCAG), and SEO best practices.

• Experience with Git, modern CI/CD workflows, and frontend testing frameworks (e.g., Jest, Playwright).

• Proactive mindset - able to identify improvement opportunities and drive them independently, not just execute assigned tasks.

• Strong problem-solving skills with the ability to identify root causes and propose pragmatic solutions in production systems.

• Collaborative team player committed to delivering high-quality outcomes.

• Excellent oral and written communication skills in English.

CREATE THE FOOTPRINTS OF TOMORROW

At ECCO, you become part of a meaningful, developing and multicultural workplace. You join a global family of more than 25,000 people who are proud to create the footprints of tomorrow.

Headquartered in Denmark, we are a family-owned company that offers international opportunities. Our offices and facilities have an informal culture and relaxed dress code – our shoe code is slightly stricter.

Join us and we guarantee lifelong learning – the speed of progress is up to you. So, if you’re curious, passionate and ready to make an impact, you’ll fit right in.

🫵 Role: Principal Data Analyst (Researcher)
📍 Location: Jakarta, Indonesia
✒️ Freelancing contract, 12 months duration
🕐 Possibility of conversion to a full-time position
📅 Deadline for applications: 31/10/2026, at midnight

Job Description

Do you have the drive and aptitude to turn ideas into reality? Do you share our passion for the environment and harnessing technology to decarbonize our society? Do you know or want to learn how environmental policy and politics can transform markets, and have an interest in sustainable transportation in Indonesia and your community? If you do, this may well be the job for you. We are seeking a Data Analyst for Indonesia. This is a role based in Indonesia, preferably Jakarta.

We are looking for a candidate who can develop and apply advanced quantitative analysis tools and techniques, synthesizing data from various sources to support our mission of creating a sustainable transport system. This could include for example total cost of ownership assessments, life-cycle analysis, and techno-economic feasibility research. The role will involve evaluating the reliability and relevance of evidence and providing objective, technical advice to shape policy and influence the public narrative on maritime (shipping) and/or road transport issues.

The ideal candidate will have a background in engineering, economics, or a related scientific field, with experience in transport and energy modeling, research, or similar areas. We are unfortunately only able to consider candidates with the unrestricted legal right to work in Indonesia. The salary package and title depend on an assessment of relevant experience.

Project Overview
This project is part of an effort to accelerate Indonesia's transition, supporting its economy-wide net zero emissions goal by 2060 or sooner. The focus is on the decarbonization of the transport sector with particular focus on the maritime and heavy duty vehicle sector.

Key Roles and Responsibilities
• Lead T&E’s analytical and research in maritime (shipping) and trucking work for Indonesia.

• Deliver economic/energy/transport modelling and/or analysis on the impacts of national and/or regional transport policy.

• Commission research and collaborate with T&E's partners in the region, ensuring that T&E’s quality standards are upheld in all deliverables.

• Write technical reports and policy briefings that detail these impacts and the policy changes that would help deliver them.

• Present research findings internally and externally.

Senior Data Analyst
Department: Analytics Department
Employment Type: Full Time
Location: Indonesia

Description
inDrive's Forecasting product turns large-scale marketplace data into daily and monthly forecasts of the company's core supply, demand and financial metrics. These forecasts are the backbone of target setting, financial planning and scenario analysis for business teams and leadership.

We are looking for a Senior Analyst to own this product: the quality and credibility of the numbers, the planning processes they feed, and the story behind every deviation. You will take over a working production solution (Python, BigQuery) and keep it reliably serving the business — but the core of the role is not modeling for its own sake. It is understanding how the business works: how pricing, incentives, marketing and market events move metrics, how those metrics connect to each other, and what decision-makers need from a forecast to plan with confidence.

Key Responsibilities
Business & planning

• Own the forecast as a decision-making product: track plan vs actual, decompose variances into business drivers (seasonality, pricing, incentives, marketing, external events), and explain in business terms why the numbers changed

• Support company planning cycles: provide forecast baselines for target setting and budgeting, and align assumptions with finance and business stakeholders

• Build and run scenario ("what-if") analysis for planned interventions: pricing changes, incentive and marketing spend, product launches, market expansion

• Maintain the dependency logic connecting supply, demand and financial metrics, so that forecasts stay mutually consistent and aggregate correctly across markets

• Translate ambiguous business questions into measurable forecasting problems; communicate assumptions, uncertainty and limitations clearly to both business and technical audiences

Forecast production

• Run and monitor recurring daily and monthly forecasts: data completeness, sanity checks, run-over-run drift

• Investigate anomalies end to end — from inputs and business transformations to forecast outputs — getting to the business reason, not just a technical fix

• Improve models pragmatically: baselines, honest validation, and model choices driven by measurable planning value rather than sophistication.

• Keep the solution maintainable: readable Python, documentation, versioned changes

Skills, Knowledge and Expertise

• 4+ years in analytics, forecasting or planning roles — for example marketplace or product analytics, demand planning, or decision science

• Strong understanding of how a business is planned: plan/fact cycles, target setting, driver-based models, unit economics. You see business metrics as a connected system, not as isolated time series

• Practical command of time-series forecasting — seasonality, holidays, external regressors, structural breaks, missing data — enough to own and improve production models

• Confident Python (pandas ecosystem): able to maintain and extend an existing production codebase

• Advanced SQL and experience with large datasets in a cloud data warehouse

• Rigorous validation habits: appropriate baselines, no data leakage, error metrics tied to business impact

• Ownership mindset: comfortable investigating issues across data, model, and integration boundaries

• Professional working proficiency in English and the ability to defend a number in front of senior stakeholders

Nice to have:

• Background in mobility, marketplaces or other supply-and-demand systems

• Experience supporting financial planning, S&OP or budgeting processes

• Econometrics and causal inference; marketing-response models (adstock, saturation, investment payback)

• Hierarchical forecasting across multiple markets

• Experience owning or supporting production batch pipelines; BigQuery, Git-based workflows, CI/CD

Technology environment
Python (pandas, NumPy, scikit-learn, Prophet), BigQuery, Databricks, Git and GitHub Actions. This is an analyst role in an engineering-friendly environment: you should be at home in this stack, but deep ML engineering is not the core of the job.

Why join us

• Help us challenge injustice by creating fair choices for millions of people across 47 countries

• Develop your professional skills with access to mentoring, career consulting, and learning programs

• Collaborate with teams around the world and gain international experience through our Global Talent Exchange Program

• Engage in company-wide challenges, awards, sports activities, employee-led social impact and volunteering projects

• Work alongside people who take initiative, speak openly, and challenge themselves to grow

• Improve your language skills through co-financed courses and internal speaking clubs

Final benefits may vary depending on the location.

Job Brief

Program Background

The Australia-Indonesia Partnership for Health Transformation (KITA SEHAT) is a joint initiative between the Governments of Australia and Indonesia to support the transformation of Indonesia’s human and animal health systems, policy, and governance. The program runs for eight years (2025–2033), with total funding of up to AUD 100 million. Phase 1 runs from August 2025 to June 2029, investing about AUD 50 million. Phase 2 will extend the program out to 2033, pending agreement between the Governments of Australia and Indonesia.

The Australia-Indonesia Partnership for Health Transformation (KITA SEHAT) is a joint initiative between the Governments of Australia and Indonesia to support the transformation of Indonesia’s human and animal health systems, policy, and governance. The program runs for eight years (2025–2033), with total funding of up to AUD 100 million. Phase 1 runs from August 2025 to June 2029, investing about AUD 50 million. Phase 2 will extend the program out to 2033, pending agreement between the Governments of Australia and Indonesia.

KITA SEHAT is funded and managed by Australia’s Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (DFAT) and implemented by DT Global. Indonesia's Ministry of National Development Planning/National Development Planning Agency (Kementerian PPN/Bappenas) is the primary coordinating ministry for the program, in partnership with the Ministry of Health, the Ministry of Agriculture and subnational governments in Jawa Barat, Nusa Tenggara Timur and Papua Barat Daya.

The program works towards four end-of-program outcomes (EOPOs):

• Primary health care policy and governance – by 2033, national and selected subnational authorities have adopted improved primary health policies, service delivery approaches and governance arrangements.

• Primary health services – by 2033, selected subnational authorities have improved the quality of and access to primary health services with a focus on stunting prevention and the inclusion of women, people with disability and other marginalised groups.

• Health system enablers – by 2033, national and selected subnational authorities have enhanced core workforce capabilities in critical human and animal health system enabling functions.

• Health security – by 2033, national and selected subnational authorities have increased capacity for health security and animal health policy development, strategic planning and the assessment, mitigation and management of acute and emerging health threats.

KITA SEHAT is designed to address local priorities, ensure women and people with disabilities are central to health system change, and to build climate resilience into how that change is delivered. The program is aligned to Indonesia’s National Medium-Term Development Plan (RPJMN) 2025-2029, specifically National Priority 4: Strengthening Human Resources Development, Science, Technology, Education, Health Sport, Gender Equality, and Strengthening the Role of Women, Youth and People with Disabilities

About DT Global Asia Pacific

At DT Global Asia Pacific, we aim to positively impact people’s lives through delivery excellence. As a leading implementing partner across Asia and the Pacific, we co-create locally led solutions in partnership with governments, communities, and stakeholders. We bring together talented teams and deep regional expertise to deliver initiatives that promote inclusive economic growth, essential services, and resilient, secure communities. With over 1,500 staff, experts in 22+ countries and more than 60 years of development experience, we tackle complex community, national and transnational challenges — from governance and justice systems to climate resilience, infrastructure and social equity — with innovative thinking and a commitment to long-term impact.

For more information, please see www.dt-global.com

The Role

KITA SEHAT seeks to strengthen primary health care (PHC) systems and services so they are more responsive to the needs of diverse population groups, including persons with disabilities. Under Intermediate Outcome (IO) 2.2 on disability-inclusive primary health services, KITA SEHAT is supporting efforts to better understand and address barriers affecting access to, utilisation of, and quality of health services for persons with disabilities and wider population.

A key requirement for advancing this work is a stronger evidence base on the health situation of persons with disabilities. Based on discussions with partner ministries, further analysis is required to understand patterns in health status, burden of disease, access to and utilisation of health services, and other relevant health outcomes among persons with disabilities. Where data allow, the analysis should also examine differences by sex, age, geography, type of disability, and other relevant characteristics to identify disparities and population groups that may experience compounded barriers to accessing quality health services.

KITA SEHAT therefore intends to engage a Data Analyst to undertake quantitative analysis of health-related data under the program’s human health portfolio, with an initial focus on disability-related health data. This will include analysis of relevant national datasets, such as the Survei Kesehatan Indonesia (SKI), alongside other appropriate data sources.

Beyond the disability-focused analysis, the Data Analyst will provide quantitative analytical support across the human health portfolio, as required. This will strengthen KITA SEHAT’s ability to measure and interpret programmatic outcomes, identify emerging trends and inequities, and translate evidence into actionable findings. The analysis will also support KITA

SEHAT’s technical assistance to government and other partners by providing a stronger evidence base for policy dialogue, program design, implementation, and recommendations.

The overall objective of the assignment is to strengthen the evidence base for KITA SEHAT and its partners’ work on disability-inclusive primary health care under IO 2.2 and wider portfolio work under ‘Human health’ themes through quantitative analysis of available population and health datasets in Indonesia.
