raw.job_description:
We’re Hiring: BI & Data Warehouse Analyst | RAIA GRID

RAIA GRID, a subsidiary of Indosat Ooredoo Hutchison, is looking for a BI & Data Warehouse Analyst to build and manage our analytical data foundation and turn data into reliable business insights.

In this role, you will design and maintain our data warehouse, develop data pipelines, and deliver reporting that teams can trust and use. You will also apply AI and machine learning to support forecasting, anomaly detection, and natural-language querying, while building the data foundation these capabilities need.

Let's be part of smarter network!

Job Description

Requirement definition and metric ownership
• Work with business owners to turn vague reporting requests into defined metrics, each with an agreed calculation, an owner, and a stated purpose.
• Maintain a single business glossary so terms such as active customer, churn, utilisation, or revenue mean one thing across every report.
• Challenge requests that duplicate existing reports, and retire dashboards nobody opens.

Data warehouse design and development
• Design and maintain dimensional models — facts, dimensions, and slowly changing dimensions — that survive changes in the source systems behind them.
• Maintain a layered warehouse structure with clear rules about what belongs in staging, integration, and presentation, and enforce those rules.
• Model data from BSS, OSS, network inventory, and finance systems into one coherent view, rather than mirroring source schemas into the warehouse.

Pipeline development and operation
• Build and schedule ELT pipelines from operational sources, including incremental loads and handling of late-arriving or corrected data.
• Monitor pipeline runs, investigate failures, and reprocess without creating duplicates or silently dropping records.
• Keep transformation logic in version control and under test, not scattered across ad hoc scripts.

Reporting and self-service enablement
• Build reports and dashboards that answer a specific decision, each with a named audience and a defined refresh frequency.
• Tune semantic models and queries so reports open quickly enough that people actually use them.
• Prepare governed datasets so business teams can answer their own questions, instead of building every report on request.

AI-enabled analytics
• Identify where AI genuinely improves an analytics outcome — forecasting, anomaly detection, classification of free-text, natural-language querying — and where conventional reporting already answers the question.
• Deliver AI-assisted analytics use cases end to end, from problem definition through to a result the business acts on.
• Build and maintain the data foundation AI depends on: clean, documented, well-modelled datasets and a semantic layer that lets a model query them reliably.
• Establish how output quality is measured before anyone is asked to trust it, including a baseline to compare against.
• Work with the AI automation function on shared standards and tooling, so the company does not end up with two conflicting approaches to AI.

Data quality and governance
• Define and automate data quality checks covering completeness, uniqueness, referential integrity, and reconciliation against source systems.
• Publish lineage so that any number in a report can be traced back to where it came from.
• Apply access controls and the requirements of UU PDP 27/2022 wherever personal data is involved, including masking in non-production environments.

Stakeholder engagement
• Present findings honestly to non-technical audiences, including what the data cannot tell them and how confident the numbers are.
• Investigate and resolve disputes about the numbers — where two reports disagree, you are the one who finds out why.
• Document models and metric definitions so the knowledge does not live only in one person's head.

Job Requirements

We care that you can build a warehouse people trust, not that you have used a specific product. Equivalent tools and experience are welcome.
• SQL: Advanced — window functions, CTEs, query tuning, and the ability to read an execution plan rather than guess at performance.
• Data modelling: Kimball dimensional modelling to a production standard; familiarity with Data Vault or wide-table approaches and a view on when each fits.
• ELT and transformation: At least one framework such as dbt, Airflow, Azure Data Factory, SSIS, Talend, Pentaho, or equivalent.
• BI platforms: Power BI, Tableau, Looker, Metabase or equivalent — including semantic modelling such as DAX or LookML, not only building charts. Power BI is directly relevant to our environment.
• Databases: Relational databases, plus a columnar or MPP warehouse such as BigQuery, Snowflake, Redshift, Synapse, or ClickHouse.
• Programming: Python for data work; Git for everything that is not a one-off query.
• Orchestration and operations: Scheduling, dependency management, monitoring, and alerting on pipeline failures.
• Cloud: At least one major cloud, with an understanding of how storage and compute costs behave as data volume grows.
• Data quality: A concrete method for testing and monitoring data correctness. This is a requirement, not a nice-to-have.
• Machine learning: Applied ML for analytics problems — forecasting, classification, anomaly detection — using standard libraries such as scikit-learn, statsmodels, or Prophet.
• LLMs in analytics: Hands-on with at least one LLM provider API, including experience exposing warehouse data to a model safely via semantic layer, generated SQL, or retrieval over documentation.
• AI system implementation: Experience taking an AI component from prototype to something that runs on a schedule, is monitored, and has an owner — covering deployment, versioning, and refresh or retraining strategy.

Valuable, not required: streaming pipelines with Kafka; data catalogue and lineage tooling; geospatial and GIS concepts in a network context; telecommunications domain data; finance reporting experience; MLOps practices; vector stores and embedding-based search; semantic layer tooling such as dbt Semantic Layer or Cube.

Experience & Qualifications
• 5–8 years in business intelligence, data warehousing, or analytics engineering. Equivalent practical experience is accepted in place of a specific degree.
• Minimum 3 years building and maintaining a data warehouse in production — not only reporting on top of one that someone else built.
• Hands-on dimensional modelling experience, with a considered view on when to depart from it.
• Ownership of at least one reporting platform used regularly by business users, including handling complaints when the numbers looked wrong.
• Experience reconciling data across several operational source systems that disagreed with each other.
• Delivered at least one AI or machine learning use case that reached regular business use — for example capacity forecasting, anomaly detection, text classification, or natural-language querying over warehouse data — and able to explain how accuracy was measured and what it was compared against.
• Practical experience using large language models in an analytics workflow, with a clear view of where they add nothing and a simpler method is better.
• Experience in telecommunications, utilities, or another asset-heavy industry is an advantage, not a requirement.

About the Role

VIDA verifies identity in real time for financial services, lending, telecommunications, and government-linked services. This makes us a target for organised fraud operations that spoof genuine users and devices at scale — and adapt within days when a defence starts working. Detection here is a continuing contest, and errors cost in both directions: missed fraud harms users and customers, while false positives deny real people access to services.

You will own detection on this path: investigate attacks in raw device and behavioural telemetry, build the rules and ML models that catch them, and measure what they catch and what they cost genuine users. The data is high-dimensional and noisy, labels are scarce and delayed, and decisions must be explainable.

What You Will Do

Understand the adversary
• Investigate real attacks — reconstruct how a campaign operates from the evidence available, and characterise it well enough that we can act on it.
• Find signal in high-dimensional, messy data — work across large volumes of device and behavioural telemetry to identify what genuinely separates fraudulent activity from legitimate users.
• Keep pace with change — when an adversary adapts, quickly establish what changed and what still distinguishes them.

Build detection that holds up
• Design detection logic and models — from feature engineering through training, calibration, and threshold selection, choosing the right tool for the problem: interpretable logic where explainability matters, models where they earn their place.
• Detect coordinated activity, not just single events — move detection beyond judging each request in isolation toward recognising organised behaviour across many, which is far harder for an adversary to disguise.
• Balance detection against user impact — treat the false-positive cost to genuine users as a first-class constraint, measured on the real population before anything is enforced.
• Own quality in production — validate before enforcement, monitor for drift and degradation, and know when to roll back.

Make the evidence trustworthy
• Build and improve ground truth — establish reliable labels in a domain where they are scarce, delayed, and imperfect, and be clear about what your labels do and do not cover.
• Hold a high evidential bar — recall and false-positive rates measured on the right populations, class imbalance, selection bias, and correctness of point-in-time evaluation. You should be able to spot the ways an analysis can flatter itself, and design around them.
• Make the work reproducible and legible — analysis and specifications that colleagues can re-run, challenge, and build on.
• Partner closely with fraud operations, engineering, and product — and communicate findings clearly to non-specialists, including when the honest answer is uncomfortable.

What We Are Looking For

Must-have
• 4+ years of applied data science or machine learning in fraud, risk, abuse, trust & safety, security, or a closely adjacent adversarial domain — with work you took to production and measured.
• Strong SQL on large datasets — comfortable and effective in large, messy event data.
• Fluent Python data-science stack — pandas, scikit-learn, and gradient-boosted trees, with clean and reproducible analysis.
• Genuine evaluation rigour — you understand why a model can look excellent offline and fail in production: label leakage, selection bias, drift, class imbalance, and the difference between conditioned and population-level error rates.
• Feature engineering from raw, semi-structured data — turning noisy, high-cardinality inputs into signals that hold up over time.
• An adversarial mindset — you instinctively ask how someone would evade what you built, and you design accordingly.
• Sound judgement on explainability — decisions affecting a person's access to services need to be defensible, not just accurate.
• Ownership and pragmatism — you can carry a problem from ambiguous question to shipped, measured outcome without waiting to be handed a specification.

Nice-to-have
• Device intelligence, device fingerprinting, or bot and automated-abuse detection.
• Biometrics, liveness, or presentation- and injection-attack detection.
• Mobile platform knowledge, including device integrity and attestation concepts.
• Graph analysis or entity resolution for linking related activity and identifying organised rings.
• Real-time or streaming features and the discipline of keeping training and serving consistent.
• Experience in emerging markets or high-growth financial services.
• Comfort using AI-assisted tooling to work faster without lowering the evidential bar.

What are we trying to solve?

We have 7.5 billion people on Earth, of which over 1 billion cannot securely prove their identity right now. Every year, 140 million babies are born, of which 40 million go unregistered. Simply put, these people are deprived of social benefits, such as education and health, their civil rights to vote and travel; and are excluded from the economy because they cannot sign up for bank accounts, loans, welfare programs etc. We believe this is unacceptable, and needs to change.

At VIDA, we are creating a frictionless digital identity system. One that fulfils the needs and expectations of our times, and is available anywhere, for everyone.

Why are we solving this problem?

The United Nations (UN) and World Bank ID4D initiatives aim to provide everyone on the planet with a legal identity by 2030. This deadline is just a few years away, we are expecting a digital identity to be a legal human right by then and we at VIDA want to be pioneers in leading this change.

Who are we?

We are a highly driven bunch of people solving this problem for our own reasons. Whether it is misleading doctors, or because we didn't get access to fair ration due to corruption — our collective goal aligns.

Who We Are

Artefact is a global consulting firm specialising in Data & AI, dedicated to transforming data into measurable business impact. We combine expertise in business consulting, Data Science, Data Engineering, Artificial Intelligence, and technology to help leading organisations accelerate their transformation.

Our multidisciplinary teams bring together Consultants, Data Scientists, Data Engineers, AI Engineers, and technology experts to develop innovative, scalable, and business-driven solutions.

We are looking for a Data Science / AI Engineer Intern who is passionate about Machine Learning, Generative AI, and emerging technologies, and eager to gain hands-on experience delivering real-world Data & AI solutions.

About the Role

As a Data Science / AI Engineer Intern, you will work alongside our Data Science and AI Engineering teams to design, develop, test, and implement data-driven and AI-powered solutions for our clients.

This role offers an opportunity to gain practical experience across Data Science, Machine Learning, Generative AI, and AI Engineering, while collaborating with multidisciplinary teams to solve real business challenges.

What You Will Be Doing
• Support the development and implementation of Data Science, Machine Learning, and AI solutions for client projects.
• Perform data collection, cleaning, preprocessing, exploratory data analysis, and feature engineering.
• Assist in building, training, evaluating, and optimising Machine Learning models.
• Explore and develop Generative AI applications, including LLMs, prompt engineering, Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), and AI agents.
• Support the development of AI prototypes, Proofs of Concept (PoCs), and practical AI applications.
• Write clean, efficient, and maintainable code, primarily using Python.
• Collaborate with Data Scientists, AI Engineers, Data Engineers, and Consultants to translate business requirements into technical solutions.
• Support model testing, validation, documentation, and deployment activities.
• Research emerging AI technologies, frameworks, and methodologies to identify potential applications for client projects.
• Communicate technical findings, project progress, and recommendations to team members and relevant stakeholders.

What We Are Looking For
• Currently pursuing or recently completed a Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Data Science, AI, Engineering, Mathematics, Statistics, or a related field.
• Good programming skills in Python, with familiarity in data manipulation and analysis.
• Foundational understanding of Machine Learning, Data Science, and Generative AI concepts.
• Strong analytical thinking, problem-solving skills, and willingness to learn new technologies.
• Good communication and collaboration skills, with a proactive and curious mindset.

What Would Give You an Advantage
• Hands-on experience with Machine Learning or AI projects through internships, academic coursework, or personal projects.
• Exposure to Generative AI technologies, such as LLMs, RAG, AI agents, Hugging Face, or LangChain.
• Familiarity with SQL, PyTorch, TensorFlow, or other Data Science and Machine Learning tools.
• Exposure to cloud platforms such as GCP, AWS, or Azure.
• Familiarity with Git, APIs, Docker, or basic MLOps practices.
• Interest in translating business challenges into practical Data & AI solutions.

Why Join Artefact?
• Hands-on Experience: Work on real-world Data Science, Machine Learning, and Generative AI projects.
• Learning & Development: Develop technical skills through practical exposure, mentorship, and collaboration with experienced Data & AI professionals.
• Emerging Technologies: Explore the latest developments in AI, LLMs, and advanced analytics.
• Multidisciplinary Collaboration: Work alongside Data Scientists, AI Engineers, Data Engineers, and Consultants.
• International Exposure: Be part of a collaborative environment connected to Artefact's regional and global network.
• Career Growth: Build a strong foundation for a future career in Data Science, AI Engineering, or Data & AI Consulting.

If you are passionate about AI, enjoy solving complex problems, and want to turn innovative ideas into practical solutions, we'd love to hear from you.

Apply through LinkedIn or visit our career page.

Artefact is the place to be: come and build the future of Data & AI with us.

• You can manage internal and external stakeholders with a collaborative, diplomatic, and flexible style.

• You work effectively in a matrixed organisation.

• You bring excellent presentation, storytelling, oral, and written communication skills.

🫵 Role: Principal Data Analyst (Researcher)
📍 Location: Jakarta, Indonesia
✒️ Freelancing contract, 12 months duration
🕐 Possibility of conversion to a full-time position
📅 Deadline for applications: 31/10/2026, at midnight

Job Description

Do you have the drive and aptitude to turn ideas into reality? Do you share our passion for the environment and harnessing technology to decarbonize our society? Do you know or want to learn how environmental policy and politics can transform markets, and have an interest in sustainable transportation in Indonesia and your community? If you do, this may well be the job for you. We are seeking a Data Analyst for Indonesia. This is a role based in Indonesia, preferably Jakarta.

We are looking for a candidate who can develop and apply advanced quantitative analysis tools and techniques, synthesizing data from various sources to support our mission of creating a sustainable transport system. This could include for example total cost of ownership assessments, life-cycle analysis, and techno-economic feasibility research. The role will involve evaluating the reliability and relevance of evidence and providing objective, technical advice to shape policy and influence the public narrative on maritime (shipping) and/or road transport issues.

The ideal candidate will have a background in engineering, economics, or a related scientific field, with experience in transport and energy modeling, research, or similar areas. We are unfortunately only able to consider candidates with the unrestricted legal right to work in Indonesia. The salary package and title depend on an assessment of relevant experience.

Project Overview
This project is part of an effort to accelerate Indonesia's transition, supporting its economy-wide net zero emissions goal by 2060 or sooner. The focus is on the decarbonization of the transport sector with particular focus on the maritime and heavy duty vehicle sector.

Key Roles and Responsibilities
• Lead T&E’s analytical and research in maritime (shipping) and trucking work for Indonesia.

• Deliver economic/energy/transport modelling and/or analysis on the impacts of national and/or regional transport policy.

• Commission research and collaborate with T&E's partners in the region, ensuring that T&E’s quality standards are upheld in all deliverables.

• Write technical reports and policy briefings that detail these impacts and the policy changes that would help deliver them.

• Present research findings internally and externally.

• Develop compelling, high quality and narrative driven graphs and data visualizations with Flourish and other interactive tools (such as netlify).

• Support T&E’s analytical work in other work programmes when additional capacity is required.

• Review T&E analytical outputs to ensure a high degree of research, analysis, and argumentation. This includes quality-assuring models, challenging input data and assumptions and interpreting output data.

• Provide input to T&E’s policy and communication strategies.

• Promote informed discussion on contemporary transport debates among T&E analysts and across the organization.

• Network with communities of transport analysts to ensure a two-way flow of relevant findings

Job requirements:
• 5+ years relevant or equivalent professional experience in transport economics/analysis, climate/energy analysis or transport policy.

• Experience or expertise in detailed quantitative analysis such as economic or transport modelling, data science or regression analysis is required. Expertise in programming (for example leveraging Python with AI tools) and/or qualitative analysis (e.g. interviews, surveys, literature reviews, content analysis) are considered a bonus.

• Excellent communication and presentation skills and an ability to write in English fluently, accurately and concisely. Other relevant languages are considered a bonus.

• Project management experience including strong interpersonal and team-working skills and an ability to deliver to tight deadlines.

• The confidence to think and act with initiative, to engage and influence policymakers, industry representatives and other stakeholders at the highest level.

Contract Duration, Location, Remuneration
• Duration: This is a one-year consultancy contract, with a high possibility of conversion to a full-time position upon successful completion of the term and depending on future project needs.

• Work Arrangement: [e.g., Consultant Contract/Flexible arrangement, including required travel for meetings/data gathering.

• The salary package and title depends on experience. We are an equal opportunities employer and offer competitive salary and benefits.

About T&E
T&E is the independent expert in enabling clean transport for all. Our vision is a zero-emissions mobility system that is affordable and has minimal impacts on our health and environment. Since we were created 30 years ago, T&E has shaped some of Europe’s most important environmental laws. We got the EU to set the world's most ambitious CO2 standards for cars and trucks but also helped uncover the Dieselgate scandal; we campaigned successfully to end palm oil diesel, secured a global ban on dirty shipping fuels and the creation of the aviation ETS, the world's largest carbon market for aviation, to name just a few.

We combine the power of robust, science-based evidence and a deep understanding of transport with powerful communications and impactful advocacy. Our staff in Brussels, Paris, Rome, Madrid, Berlin, Warsaw and London collaborate with our 49 national members. From 2024, T&E has been enhancing our collaboration between Asia and Europe, starting from our Singapore office, to accelerate zero-emission transport and energy transition, helping ensure that global decarbonization efforts are both inclusive and regionally grounded. Altogether, our members represent more than 3.5 million people.

⚠️ IMPORTANT SECURITY NOTICE FOR APPLICANTS
Protecting Your Personal Data against Recruitment Scams: T&E takes digital data privacy and information security seriously. Please note that all legitimate communication from our talent acquisition team will exclusively originate from an official corporate domain ending in @transportenvironment.org (or cleancitiescampaign.org) or directly via secure automated channels on our managed applicant tracking platform.

• No Unverified Communication: T&E does not authorize external recruitment agencies or headhunters to contact candidates using unverified, generic webmail accounts such as @gmail.com, @yahoo.com, or @outlook.com.

• No Charging or Fees: T&E will never request sensitive financial information, banking credentials, passport copies, or any form of payment at any stage of our recruitment process.

• Verification Protocol: All legitimate T&E vacancies are listed on our 2 websites https://jobs.transportenvironment.org/ or https://cleancitiescampaign.org/vacancies/

If you receive a suspicious solicitation and wish to verify its legitimacy, please cross-reference the vacancy on our 2 websites or forward the communication directly to the HR team at hrsupport@transportenvironment.org before sharing any personal documentation.

Get to Know the Team

GrabFin Analytics team supports the GFin product and business organisations, across Payments, Lending, Insurance, and Kios. As a Senior Data Scientist (Analytics), you will be part of the Lending tech family where we strive to be the best FinTech company in the region. Our team is focused on understanding user experiences and partnering with Business, Product, Design, and Tech teams to achieve the right outcomes. We are integral to product development, from understanding user journeys with UX designers, to developing hypotheses, through to post-rollout optimisation.

Get to Know the Role

In this role, you'll partner closely with Product Managers to turn product and business questions into clear hypotheses, thoughtfully designed experiments, and actionable insights. You'll build a deep understanding of users—their needs, pain points, and behaviours—while keeping business goals in view. As a strategic analytics partner throughout the product development lifecycle, you'll support teams from early ideation through execution, helping shape product direction and prioritize features based on evidence and expected impact.

The Critical Tasks You Will Perform
• Partner with cross-functional teams to identify data requirements and design innovative analytical solutions or insights to address complex challenges effectively.
• Conduct in-depth analyses of operational data, including business/impact analysis and text analysis, to identify areas for improvement and process optimization.
• Develop dashboards to monitor the performance of Grab Support operations, support specialists, and the business overall.
• Utilize advanced statistical and machine learning techniques, such as quasi-experimental methods, NLP & LLM, to analyze large datasets and derive meaningful insights that drive business decisions, improve support performance, and mitigate risks.
• Stay up-to-date with industry trends, emerging technologies, and best practices in analytics and data science, leveraging this knowledge to enhance the organization's data-driven capabilities.
• Collaborate with data engineering teams to ensure data quality, integrity, and accessibility, while building data pipelines and infrastructure for analytics projects.
• Communicate complex analytical findings to all stakeholders, including senior management, through concise reports, presentations, and visualizations.

What Essential Skills You Will Need
• A minimum of Bachelor's degree in Analytics, Statistics, or Engineering or any related field.
• At least 2+ years of experience in Analytics, Business Intelligence, or Data Science roles, preferably in an Internet or "Direct-to-Consumer" company with large, complex, high-velocity data.
• Proficiency in Big Data technologies such as Spark, PySpark, and Databricks.
• Strong foundation in data query/manipulation using SQL and data visualization tools like Power BI.
• Experience in Snowflake and multidimensional modeling .

Life at Grab

We care about your well-being at Grab, here are some of the global benefits we offer:
• We have your back with Term Life Insurance and comprehensive Medical Insurance.
• With GrabFlex, create a benefits package that suits your needs and aspirations.
• Celebrate moments that matter in life with loved ones through Parental and Birthday leave, and give back to your communities through Love-all-Serve-all (LASA) volunteering leave
• We have a confidential Grabber Assistance Programme to guide and uplift you and your loved ones through life's challenges.
• Balancing personal commitments and life's demands are made easier with our FlexWork arrangements such as differentiated hours

What We Stand For At Grab

We are committed to building an inclusive and equitable workplace that provides equal opportunity for Grabbers to grow and perform at their best. We consider all candidates fairly and equally regardless of nationality, ethnicity, race, religion, age, gender, family commitments, physical and mental impairments or disabilities, and other attributes that make them unique.

Join Neurons Lab as a Data Engineer (part-time) on a flagship engagement with a European private investment group — a holding company with a C-level executive team, an investment/portfolio function and an affiliated family office.

The programme builds one private, access-scoped context layer over the group's data, then AI skills and agents on top of it. You build the plumbing underneath: Phase 1 (Capture) — turn on ingestion across calls, email, Slack and messengers, board protocols, decks and portfolio updates, live and historical; Phase 2 (Connect) — land it all in the context layer with identity resolved, access scope attached and lineage intact.

This is deliberately an unstructured-first data-engineering role. There is no clean warehouse to model: the raw material is transcripts, threads, attachments and years of archive, and the hard problems are entity resolution across people and entities, deduplication, incremental sync, PII handling, and keeping cost sane at volume.

Roughly eight to ten two-week sprints overall, with your load front-weighted to the first four or five — allocation may flex above 0.5 FTE during Capture and Connect and settle back afterwards.

Stage: active project, start ASAP.

Part-time, 20 to 30 hours-a-week engagement.

What you'll actually do (example tasks)

• Stand up capture by default: notetaker on every call with speaker attribution, plus ingestion from mail, Slack and messengers — designed as opt-out, not opt-in, and reversible if the client changes their mind.

• Backfill the archive: years of historical email, Slack, board protocols, decks and portfolio updates — parsed, deduplicated and dated correctly.

• Build document parsing for the awkward long tail: PDFs, scanned board packs, spreadsheets, slide decks, forwarded attachments.

• Implement identity / entity resolution: the same person across Slack handle, mail alias and calendar invite; the same portfolio company across a deck, a mail thread and a CRM record.

• Build chunking and embedding pipelines and load the vector + graph stores behind the ontology the architect defines.

• Implement incremental sync through the connector layer (MCP / Composio-class) — no full re-crawls, no silent drift, clear handling of edits and deletions.

• Attach access scope and provenance to every record at ingestion, so permission-aware retrieval and audit are possible downstream rather than bolted on.

• Run PII detection, redaction and retention logic; evidence to the client's security function what is stored, where, and for how long.

• Orchestrate with Airflow / Step Functions; build repeatable, monitored pipelines rather than scripts, with alerting when a source stops flowing.

• Keep cost and latency under control at volume — batching, incremental embedding, storage tiering — and report the unit economics.

• Write runbooks so the client's own team can operate this after handover.

Skills

• Strong Python and solid SQL

• Unstructured-data pipelines: transcripts, mail, chat, documents — parsing, normalisation, deduplication

• Embedding / retrieval infrastructure: chunking strategies, vector stores (pgvector, OpenSearch, Pinecone-class), plus loading a graph store

• API and connector integration at scale: Google Workspace / M365, Slack, CRM; rate limits, pagination, incremental cursors, webhooks

• Entity resolution / record linkage (deterministic + fuzzy) without a clean shared key

• Orchestration: Airflow, Step Functions or equivalent; idempotent, restartable jobs

• AWS and/or GCP data stack; comfortable in a private / VPC deployment

• PII detection, redaction, encryption and retention in practice

• Clear written English; documents for handover and works well async in a small distributed pod

Knowledge

• GDPR applied to employee-generated data (mail, chat, meeting recordings) and EU data residency across multiple jurisdictions

• Data lineage, provenance and audit patterns — and why an AI system needs them more, not less

• How retrieval quality depends on ingestion quality — enough understanding of RAG to make the right upstream choices

• Well-Architected security and cost practice; awareness of financial-services expectations — a plus

Experience

• 4+ years in data engineering, with real unstructured / semi-structured work (not only warehouse modelling)

• Demonstrated experience integrating many third-party APIs into one coherent store, including historical backfill

• Experience building pipelines feeding an LLM / retrieval system — strong plus

• Experience handling sensitive personal data in a regulated or security-sensitive environment

• Comfortable being the only data engineer on a small (2.5-FTE) pod, at part-time allocation, without hand-holding

Get to Know the Team

The Enterprise Data Analytics (EDA) team, part of Grab's Analytics function, owns the data behind Grab's regulatory obligations across Southeast Asia. We build and run the data pipelines that produce regulatory reports for financial regulators, including OJK and Bank Indonesia, Bank Negara Malaysia, the Monetary Authority of Singapore, Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas and the Bank of Thailand. We also support AML transaction monitoring and regulatory audits, working closely with Country Compliance, AML and Fraud, Risk, Finance and Engineering. Our numbers go to regulators, so accuracy, traceability and on-time delivery come first.

Get to Know the Role

As the Senior Data Analyst, you will be the analytics owner of regulatory reporting for Grab's e-money, payments and P2P lending businesses in Indonesia. You will take each report end to end, from interpreting the regulation to delivering a validated output to Compliance for submission, and be the go-to person when Compliance, auditors or regulators ask how a number was produced. You will report into the Analytics Manager, Compliance, and work onsite at our Jakarta office.

The Critical Tasks You Will Perform
• You will take end-to-end ownership of daily, weekly and monthly regulatory reports for OJK, Bank Indonesia and industry bodies, such as SLIK, Pusdafil, APOLO and fintech data centre reporting, delivering them accurately and on time.
• You will translate new and changed regulations into documented data requirements, definitions and pipeline changes, agreeing the interpretation with Compliance before go-live.
• You will reconcile regulatory outputs against Finance records and across related reports, find the root cause of discrepancies, and automate data-quality checks to replace manual reconciliation.
• You will build and maintain reliable, reproducible reporting pipelines on Airflow and Spark, and resolve failures and source-data changes before submission deadlines.
• You will assess the reporting impact of product launches, system migrations and source-data changes, and partner with Engineering to test them before cut-over.
• You will provide traceable, transaction-level analysis for regulatory audits, regulator data requests and AML transaction monitoring.
• You will communicate data issues and their impact to mid-to-senior Compliance, Finance and Risk partners, and mentor junior analysts on reporting best practices.
• You will build AI tools and self-serve solutions that speed up report development and validation, while keeping confidential data protected.

What Essential Skills You Will Need
• You have at least 4 years of experience in Analytics, Business Intelligence or Data Science in regulatory reporting, compliance or risk at a FinTech company or Financial Institution.
• You have a Bachelor's Degree in Statistics, Mathematics, Computer Science, Economics, Engineering or related fields.
• You are proficient in writing advanced SQL queries (Presto, Spark SQL or Hive) on large datasets, and in Python for automating analysis and data pipelines.
• You have hands-on experience building and operating scheduled data pipelines with Airflow or a similar orchestrator.
• You have a strong track record of reconciliations and data-quality controls, and can trace a discrepancy across systems to its source.
• You have working knowledge of Indonesian financial regulation and reporting (OJK, Bank Indonesia or AFPI) or of AML/CFT data.
• You can turn regulatory text into clear data logic and explain it to non-technical partners such as compliance officers and auditors.
• Full professional working proficiency in English is required, on top of fluency in Bahasa Indonesia.

Life at Grab

• We have your back with Term Life Insurance and comprehensive Medical Insurance.

Role Overview

As a Senior SRE Engineer II at Ajaib, you own the reliability of production services and platforms end to end: observability, incident response, infrastructure as code, Kubernetes, releases and capacity. You work with product engineering teams to keep trading, payment and money systems available and fast, lead incidents when they happen, remove manual work through automation, and help the engineers around you grow.

• Own the reliability of services and platforms: define SLOs with product teams, track them and act when they are at risk
• Build and improve monitoring, logging, tracing and alerting so that problems are found quickly and alerts are useful and not noisy

Requirements

• Infrastructure: Strong experience with Kubernetes, infrastructure as code (Terraform) and a major cloud platform (GCP or AWS)

• Systems Fundamentals: Strong Linux, networking (DNS, TLS, load balancing) and troubleshooting skills
• Data & Messaging Operations: Working experience operating relational databases, Kafka or Redis
• Mindset & Domain: Ownership mindset and clear communication. Experience in fintech or another regulated, high-traffic environment is a strong plus

Benefits

• Learning & Development - Company-sponsored training, courses, and professional certifications
• Hybrid Work Arrangement - Enjoy the flexibility of working both remotely and from the office
• Career Growth - Work closely with experienced leaders and take on meaningful ownership as we scale
• Employee Perks - Enjoy exclusive discounts, partnerships, and lifestyle perks

Job Description

Do you have the drive and aptitude to turn ideas into reality? Do you share our passion for the environment and harnessing technology to decarbonize our society? Do you know or want to learn how environmental policy and politics can transform markets, and have an interest in sustainable transportation in Indonesia and your community? If you do, this may well be the job for you. We are seeking a Data Analyst for Indonesia. This is a role based in Indonesia, preferably Jakarta.

We are looking for a candidate who can develop and apply advanced quantitative analysis tools and techniques, synthesizing data from various sources to support our mission of creating a sustainable transport system. This could include for example total cost of ownership assessments, life-cycle analysis, and techno-economic feasibility research. The role will involve evaluating the reliability and relevance of evidence and providing objective, technical advice to shape policy and influence the public narrative on maritime (shipping) and/or road transport issues.

The ideal candidate will have a background in engineering, economics, or a related scientific field, with experience in transport and energy modeling, research, or similar areas. We are unfortunately only able to consider candidates with the unrestricted legal right to work in Indonesia. The salary package and title depend on an assessment of relevant experience.

Project Overview
This project is part of an effort to accelerate Indonesia's transition, supporting its economy-wide net zero emissions goal by 2060 or sooner. The focus is on the decarbonization of the transport sector with particular focus on the maritime and heavy duty vehicle sector.

Key Roles and Responsibilities
• Lead T&E’s analytical and research in maritime (shipping) and trucking work for Indonesia.

• Deliver economic/energy/transport modelling and/or analysis on the impacts of national and/or regional transport policy.

• Commission research and collaborate with T&E's partners in the region, ensuring that T&E’s quality standards are upheld in all deliverables.

• Write technical reports and policy briefings that detail these impacts and the policy changes that would help deliver them.

• Present research findings internally and externally.

• Develop compelling, high quality and narrative driven graphs and data visualizations with Flourish and other interactive tools (such as netlify).

• Support T&E’s analytical work in other work programmes when additional capacity is required.

• Review T&E analytical outputs to ensure a high degree of research, analysis, and argumentation. This includes quality-assuring models, challenging input data and assumptions and interpreting output data.

• Provide input to T&E’s policy and communication strategies.

• Promote informed discussion on contemporary transport debates among T&E analysts and across the organization.

• Network with communities of transport analysts to ensure a two-way flow of relevant findings

Job requirements:
• 5+ years relevant or equivalent professional experience in transport economics/analysis, climate/energy analysis or transport policy.

Job Brief

Data Analyst GEDSI (Short Term Advisor) Location: Jakarta, Indonesia

Program Background

The Australia-Indonesia Partnership for Health Transformation (KITA SEHAT) is a joint initiative between the Governments of Australia and Indonesia to support the transformation of Indonesia’s human and animal health systems, policy, and governance. The program runs for eight years (2025–2033), with total funding of up to AUD 100 million. Phase 1 runs from August 2025 to June 2029, investing about AUD 50 million. Phase 2 will extend the program out to 2033, pending agreement between the Governments of Australia and Indonesia.

The Australia-Indonesia Partnership for Health Transformation (KITA SEHAT) is a joint initiative between the Governments of Australia and Indonesia to support the transformation of Indonesia’s human and animal health systems, policy, and governance. The program runs for eight years (2025–2033), with total funding of up to AUD 100 million. Phase 1 runs from August 2025 to June 2029, investing about AUD 50 million. Phase 2 will extend the program out to 2033, pending agreement between the Governments of Australia and Indonesia.

KITA SEHAT is funded and managed by Australia’s Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (DFAT) and implemented by DT Global. Indonesia's Ministry of National Development Planning/National Development Planning Agency (Kementerian PPN/Bappenas) is the primary coordinating ministry for the program, in partnership with the Ministry of Health, the Ministry of Agriculture and subnational governments in Jawa Barat, Nusa Tenggara Timur and Papua Barat Daya.

The program works towards four end-of-program outcomes (EOPOs):

• Primary health care policy and governance – by 2033, national and selected subnational authorities have adopted improved primary health policies, service delivery approaches and governance arrangements.

• Primary health services – by 2033, selected subnational authorities have improved the quality of and access to primary health services with a focus on stunting prevention and the inclusion of women, people with disability and other marginalised groups.

• Health system enablers – by 2033, national and selected subnational authorities have enhanced core workforce capabilities in critical human and animal health system enabling functions.

• Health security – by 2033, national and selected subnational authorities have increased capacity for health security and animal health policy development, strategic planning and the assessment, mitigation and management of acute and emerging health threats.

KITA SEHAT is designed to address local priorities, ensure women and people with disabilities are central to health system change, and to build climate resilience into how that change is delivered. The program is aligned to Indonesia’s National Medium-Term Development Plan (RPJMN) 2025-2029, specifically National Priority 4: Strengthening Human Resources Development, Science, Technology, Education, Health Sport, Gender Equality, and Strengthening the Role of Women, Youth and People with Disabilities

About DT Global Asia Pacific

At DT Global Asia Pacific, we aim to positively impact people’s lives through delivery excellence. As a leading implementing partner across Asia and the Pacific, we co-create locally led solutions in partnership with governments, communities, and stakeholders. We bring together talented teams and deep regional expertise to deliver initiatives that promote inclusive economic growth, essential services, and resilient, secure communities. With over 1,500 staff, experts in 22+ countries and more than 60 years of development experience, we tackle complex community, national and transnational challenges — from governance and justice systems to climate resilience, infrastructure and social equity — with innovative thinking and a commitment to long-term impact.

For more information, please see www.dt-global.com

The Role

KITA SEHAT seeks to strengthen primary health care (PHC) systems and services so they are more responsive to the needs of diverse population groups, including persons with disabilities. Under Intermediate Outcome (IO) 2.2 on disability-inclusive primary health services, KITA SEHAT is supporting efforts to better understand and address barriers affecting access to, utilisation of, and quality of health services for persons with disabilities and wider population.

A key requirement for advancing this work is a stronger evidence base on the health situation of persons with disabilities. Based on discussions with partner ministries, further analysis is required to understand patterns in health status, burden of disease, access to and utilisation of health services, and other relevant health outcomes among persons with disabilities. Where data allow, the analysis should also examine differences by sex, age, geography, type of disability, and other relevant characteristics to identify disparities and population groups that may experience compounded barriers to accessing quality health services.

KITA SEHAT therefore intends to engage a Data Analyst to undertake quantitative analysis of health-related data under the program’s human health portfolio, with an initial focus on disability-related health data. This will include analysis of relevant national datasets, such as the Survei Kesehatan Indonesia (SKI), alongside other appropriate data sources.

Beyond the disability-focused analysis, the Data Analyst will provide quantitative analytical support across the human health portfolio, as required. This will strengthen KITA SEHAT’s ability to measure and interpret programmatic outcomes, identify emerging trends and inequities, and translate evidence into actionable findings. The analysis will also support KITA

SEHAT’s technical assistance to government and other partners by providing a stronger evidence base for policy dialogue, program design, implementation, and recommendations.

The overall objective of the assignment is to strengthen the evidence base for KITA SEHAT and its partners’ work on disability-inclusive primary health care under IO 2.2 and wider portfolio work under ‘Human health’ themes through quantitative analysis of available population and health datasets in Indonesia.

Senior Data Analyst
Department: Analytics Department
Employment Type: Full Time
Location: Indonesia

Description
inDrive's Forecasting product turns large-scale marketplace data into daily and monthly forecasts of the company's core supply, demand and financial metrics. These forecasts are the backbone of target setting, financial planning and scenario analysis for business teams and leadership.

We are looking for a Senior Analyst to own this product: the quality and credibility of the numbers, the planning processes they feed, and the story behind every deviation. You will take over a working production solution (Python, BigQuery) and keep it reliably serving the business — but the core of the role is not modeling for its own sake. It is understanding how the business works: how pricing, incentives, marketing and market events move metrics, how those metrics connect to each other, and what decision-makers need from a forecast to plan with confidence.

Key Responsibilities
Business & planning

• Own the forecast as a decision-making product: track plan vs actual, decompose variances into business drivers (seasonality, pricing, incentives, marketing, external events), and explain in business terms why the numbers changed

• Support company planning cycles: provide forecast baselines for target setting and budgeting, and align assumptions with finance and business stakeholders

• Build and run scenario ("what-if") analysis for planned interventions: pricing changes, incentive and marketing spend, product launches, market expansion

• Maintain the dependency logic connecting supply, demand and financial metrics, so that forecasts stay mutually consistent and aggregate correctly across markets

• Translate ambiguous business questions into measurable forecasting problems; communicate assumptions, uncertainty and limitations clearly to both business and technical audiences

Forecast production

• Run and monitor recurring daily and monthly forecasts: data completeness, sanity checks, run-over-run drift

• Investigate anomalies end to end — from inputs and business transformations to forecast outputs — getting to the business reason, not just a technical fix

• Improve models pragmatically: baselines, honest validation, and model choices driven by measurable planning value rather than sophistication.

• Keep the solution maintainable: readable Python, documentation, versioned changes

Skills, Knowledge and Expertise

• 4+ years in analytics, forecasting or planning roles — for example marketplace or product analytics, demand planning, or decision science

• Strong understanding of how a business is planned: plan/fact cycles, target setting, driver-based models, unit economics. You see business metrics as a connected system, not as isolated time series

• Practical command of time-series forecasting — seasonality, holidays, external regressors, structural breaks, missing data — enough to own and improve production models

• Confident Python (pandas ecosystem): able to maintain and extend an existing production codebase

• Advanced SQL and experience with large datasets in a cloud data warehouse

• Rigorous validation habits: appropriate baselines, no data leakage, error metrics tied to business impact

• Ownership mindset: comfortable investigating issues across data, model, and integration boundaries

• Professional working proficiency in English and the ability to defend a number in front of senior stakeholders

Nice to have:

• Background in mobility, marketplaces or other supply-and-demand systems

• Experience supporting financial planning, S&OP or budgeting processes

• Econometrics and causal inference; marketing-response models (adstock, saturation, investment payback)

• Hierarchical forecasting across multiple markets

• Experience owning or supporting production batch pipelines; BigQuery, Git-based workflows, CI/CD

Technology environment
Python (pandas, NumPy, scikit-learn, Prophet), BigQuery, Databricks, Git and GitHub Actions. This is an analyst role in an engineering-friendly environment: you should be at home in this stack, but deep ML engineering is not the core of the job.

Why join us

• Help us challenge injustice by creating fair choices for millions of people across 47 countries

• Develop your professional skills with access to mentoring, career consulting, and learning programs

• Collaborate with teams around the world and gain international experience through our Global Talent Exchange Program

• Engage in company-wide challenges, awards, sports activities, employee-led social impact and volunteering projects

• Work alongside people who take initiative, speak openly, and challenge themselves to grow

• Improve your language skills through co-financed courses and internal speaking clubs

Final benefits may vary depending on the location.

raw.job_description:
We’re Hiring: BI & Data Warehouse Analyst | RAIA GRID

RAIA GRID, a subsidiary of Indosat Ooredoo Hutchison, is looking for a BI & Data Warehouse Analyst to build and manage our analytical data foundation and turn data into reliable business insights.

In this role, you will design and maintain our data warehouse, develop data pipelines, and deliver reporting that teams can trust and use. You will also apply AI and machine learning to support forecasting, anomaly detection, and natural-language querying, while building the data foundation these capabilities need.

Let's be part of smarter network!

Job Description

Requirement definition and metric ownership
• Work with business owners to turn vague reporting requests into defined metrics, each with an agreed calculation, an owner, and a stated purpose.
• Maintain a single business glossary so terms such as active customer, churn, utilisation, or revenue mean one thing across every report.
• Challenge requests that duplicate existing reports, and retire dashboards nobody opens.

Data warehouse design and development
• Design and maintain dimensional models — facts, dimensions, and slowly changing dimensions — that survive changes in the source systems behind them.
• Maintain a layered warehouse structure with clear rules about what belongs in staging, integration, and presentation, and enforce those rules.
• Model data from BSS, OSS, network inventory, and finance systems into one coherent view, rather than mirroring source schemas into the warehouse.

Pipeline development and operation
• Build and schedule ELT pipelines from operational sources, including incremental loads and handling of late-arriving or corrected data.
• Monitor pipeline runs, investigate failures, and reprocess without creating duplicates or silently dropping records.
• Keep transformation logic in version control and under test, not scattered across ad hoc scripts.

Reporting and self-service enablement
• Build reports and dashboards that answer a specific decision, each with a named audience and a defined refresh frequency.
• Tune semantic models and queries so reports open quickly enough that people actually use them.
• Prepare governed datasets so business teams can answer their own questions, instead of building every report on request.

AI-enabled analytics
• Identify where AI genuinely improves an analytics outcome — forecasting, anomaly detection, classification of free-text, natural-language querying — and where conventional reporting already answers the question.
• Deliver AI-assisted analytics use cases end to end, from problem definition through to a result the business acts on.
• Build and maintain the data foundation AI depends on: clean, documented, well-modelled datasets and a semantic layer that lets a model query them reliably.
• Establish how output quality is measured before anyone is asked to trust it, including a baseline to compare against.
• Work with the AI automation function on shared standards and tooling, so the company does not end up with two conflicting approaches to AI.

Data quality and governance
• Define and automate data quality checks covering completeness, uniqueness, referential integrity, and reconciliation against source systems.
• Publish lineage so that any number in a report can be traced back to where it came from.
• Apply access controls and the requirements of UU PDP 27/2022 wherever personal data is involved, including masking in non-production environments.

Stakeholder engagement
• Present findings honestly to non-technical audiences, including what the data cannot tell them and how confident the numbers are.
• Investigate and resolve disputes about the numbers — where two reports disagree, you are the one who finds out why.
• Document models and metric definitions so the knowledge does not live only in one person's head.

Job Requirements

We care that you can build a warehouse people trust, not that you have used a specific product. Equivalent tools and experience are welcome.
• SQL: Advanced — window functions, CTEs, query tuning, and the ability to read an execution plan rather than guess at performance.
• Data modelling: Kimball dimensional modelling to a production standard; familiarity with Data Vault or wide-table approaches and a view on when each fits.
• ELT and transformation: At least one framework such as dbt, Airflow, Azure Data Factory, SSIS, Talend, Pentaho, or equivalent.
• BI platforms: Power BI, Tableau, Looker, Metabase or equivalent — including semantic modelling such as DAX or LookML, not only building charts. Power BI is directly relevant to our environment.
• Databases: Relational databases, plus a columnar or MPP warehouse such as BigQuery, Snowflake, Redshift, Synapse, or ClickHouse.
• Programming: Python for data work; Git for everything that is not a one-off query.
• Orchestration and operations: Scheduling, dependency management, monitoring, and alerting on pipeline failures.
• Cloud: At least one major cloud, with an understanding of how storage and compute costs behave as data volume grows.
• Data quality: A concrete method for testing and monitoring data correctness. This is a requirement, not a nice-to-have.
• Machine learning: Applied ML for analytics problems — forecasting, classification, anomaly detection — using standard libraries such as scikit-learn, statsmodels, or Prophet.
• LLMs in analytics: Hands-on with at least one LLM provider API, including experience exposing warehouse data to a model safely via semantic layer, generated SQL, or retrieval over documentation.
• AI system implementation: Experience taking an AI component from prototype to something that runs on a schedule, is monitored, and has an owner — covering deployment, versioning, and refresh or retraining strategy.

Valuable, not required: streaming pipelines with Kafka; data catalogue and lineage tooling; geospatial and GIS concepts in a network context; telecommunications domain data; finance reporting experience; MLOps practices; vector stores and embedding-based search; semantic layer tooling such as dbt Semantic Layer or Cube.

Experience & Qualifications
• 5–8 years in business intelligence, data warehousing, or analytics engineering. Equivalent practical experience is accepted in place of a specific degree.
• Minimum 3 years building and maintaining a data warehouse in production — not only reporting on top of one that someone else built.
• Hands-on dimensional modelling experience, with a considered view on when to depart from it.
• Ownership of at least one reporting platform used regularly by business users, including handling complaints when the numbers looked wrong.
• Experience reconciling data across several operational source systems that disagreed with each other.
• Delivered at least one AI or machine learning use case that reached regular business use — for example capacity forecasting, anomaly detection, text classification, or natural-language querying over warehouse data — and able to explain how accuracy was measured and what it was compared against.
• Practical experience using large language models in an analytics workflow, with a clear view of where they add nothing and a simpler method is better.
• Experience in telecommunications, utilities, or another asset-heavy industry is an advantage, not a requirement.

Who are we?

Amar Bank is one of the most technologically advanced digital banks in Indonesia. Our leading

digital lending product, Tunaiku has the distinction of being the first FinTech product in

Indonesia. We are also the first digital bank on the cloud. As the first profitable digital bank, we

managed to get listed on the Indonesian Stock Exchange.

How did we manage to do that?

We are changing people’s perception of a bank. We believe we are the innovators who combine

customer focus principles with creating technology-based impact. We incorporate freedom and

flexibility as part of our startup working culture DNA to encourage innovation in creating better

financial solutions for the banking industry. We think of ourselves as, ‘A technology company

with a banking license’. For this reason, we ‘Act like a FinTech, and think like a Bank.’

How did it all start?

Founded on March 15, 1991, in Surabaya as PT Anglomas International Bank (Amin Bank), the

bank was acquired by Tolaram Group and transformed to PT Bank Amar Indonesia (Amar Bank)

in 2014. It has then undergone a significant digital transformation to become one of the

country's forerunning fintech institutions through its award-winning digital lending platform,

Tunaiku.

Our philosophy, mission, and vision

Technology must impact lives, must improve lives. We exist to provide banking to those who

We're looking for a modern, detail-obsessed UI/UX & Visual Designer to shape the look and feel of White Code Labs across our website and software products on web and mobile. • Strong communication skills and the ability to work independently.

• Experience with motion and micro-interactions using tools such as After Effects, Lottie, or Rive is a plus.

• Experience with AI image-generation and design tools is a plus.

Benefits

• Real ownership of the visual experience across our website and software products.

• Freedom to bring creative ideas to life and influence how complex technology is presented.

Minimum 3 years of professional experience shipping fullstack features in production, or equivalent demonstrable skill.

Can build and ship a feature across the whole stack: the API, the screen that uses it, the data behind it, and the tests. Our internal platform is a Ruby on Rails API, Express.js and a React (TypeScript) web app; fullstack experience in any comparable stack transfers in fast, Rails included.

A shipped fullstack project (production, personal, or open source) you can walk us through and defend.

Elite frontend polish. You must be able to build the UI for your module, but the backend is your depth.

On our delivery squads, every engineer owns a module across the whole stack, its API, its UI, its data, and its tests, and carries it from prototype to working, tested software.

Depth is where you go deeper than the rest of the squad, while still owning your module end to end. Your depth is the backend: the modules with hard server-side architecture such as AI engines, integrations, ETL, and algorithmic cores. When a module has a difficult backend core, it comes to you, and you build its UI, its data, and its tests too, like every fullstack owner. You are the person the squad trusts with the hard backend problem, and you keep building the rest of the module yourself.

From day one, you own real modules on live client squads and on internal product, at a scope matched to your experience: routine-to-common backend complexity you run independently, with a Technical Lead or a more senior fullstack engineer backing you on the hardest architecture calls. As your backend mastery deepens, the scope you own grows with it, on a clear path toward owning the seat’s hardest backend cores outright.

What you will do

Own a module across the whole stack: build its API, its UI, its data layer, and its tests. You finish a whole feature.

Take the modules where the backend is the hard part (AI engines, integrations, ETL, algorithmic cores) and go deep there, while still delivering the rest of the module yourself.

Write the tests for what you build, from week one, as continuous regression.

Turn a Definition of Done and a clickable prototype into working, traceable software, on real client engagements.

Join story kickoffs and walk the acceptance criteria and edge cases before you write code.

Work on AI features (for example a report-generation or extraction flow) alongside the Technical Lead, and learn how they move through the three AI stages: proof of concept, core function integrated end to end, and measurable outcome.

Use AI heavily to move fast, then verify. Generating a thousand lines of plausible code is cheap. Knowing whether it is correct is the skill.

What you own now

Modules built fullstack, end to end, at routine-to-common backend complexity: API, UI, data, and tests, traced to a requirement.

Your module’s defects and its demo.

Who you will work with

Reports to: Technical Lead. Hiring decision: CTO.

You get a Definition of Done and a prototype from the product and tech layers, you give honest constraint signals early, and you hand the SDET a module that is testable in CI.

🫵 Role: Principal Data Analyst (Researcher)
📍 Location: Jakarta, Indonesia
✒️ Freelancing contract, 12 months duration
🕐 Possibility of conversion to a full-time position
📅 Deadline for applications: 31/10/2026, at midnight

Job Description

Do you have the drive and aptitude to turn ideas into reality? Do you share our passion for the environment and harnessing technology to decarbonize our society? Do you know or want to learn how environmental policy and politics can transform markets, and have an interest in sustainable transportation in Indonesia and your community? If you do, this may well be the job for you. We are seeking a Data Analyst for Indonesia. This is a role based in Indonesia, preferably Jakarta.

We are looking for a candidate who can develop and apply advanced quantitative analysis tools and techniques, synthesizing data from various sources to support our mission of creating a sustainable transport system. This could include for example total cost of ownership assessments, life-cycle analysis, and techno-economic feasibility research. The role will involve evaluating the reliability and relevance of evidence and providing objective, technical advice to shape policy and influence the public narrative on maritime (shipping) and/or road transport issues.

The ideal candidate will have a background in engineering, economics, or a related scientific field, with experience in transport and energy modeling, research, or similar areas. We are unfortunately only able to consider candidates with the unrestricted legal right to work in Indonesia. The salary package and title depend on an assessment of relevant experience.

Project Overview
This project is part of an effort to accelerate Indonesia's transition, supporting its economy-wide net zero emissions goal by 2060 or sooner. The focus is on the decarbonization of the transport sector with particular focus on the maritime and heavy duty vehicle sector.

Key Roles and Responsibilities
• Lead T&E’s analytical and research in maritime (shipping) and trucking work for Indonesia.

• Deliver economic/energy/transport modelling and/or analysis on the impacts of national and/or regional transport policy.

• Commission research and collaborate with T&E's partners in the region, ensuring that T&E’s quality standards are upheld in all deliverables.

• Write technical reports and policy briefings that detail these impacts and the policy changes that would help deliver them.

• Present research findings internally and externally.

• Develop compelling, high quality and narrative driven graphs and data visualizations with Flourish and other interactive tools (such as netlify).

• Support T&E’s analytical work in other work programmes when additional capacity is required.

• Review T&E analytical outputs to ensure a high degree of research, analysis, and argumentation. This includes quality-assuring models, challenging input data and assumptions and interpreting output data.

• Provide input to T&E’s policy and communication strategies.

• Promote informed discussion on contemporary transport debates among T&E analysts and across the organization.

• Network with communities of transport analysts to ensure a two-way flow of relevant findings

Job requirements:
• 5+ years relevant or equivalent professional experience in transport economics/analysis, climate/energy analysis or transport policy.

• Experience or expertise in detailed quantitative analysis such as economic or transport modelling, data science or regression analysis is required. Expertise in programming (for example leveraging Python with AI tools) and/or qualitative analysis (e.g. interviews, surveys, literature reviews, content analysis) are considered a bonus.

• Excellent communication and presentation skills and an ability to write in English fluently, accurately and concisely. Other relevant languages are considered a bonus.

• Project management experience including strong interpersonal and team-working skills and an ability to deliver to tight deadlines.

• The confidence to think and act with initiative, to engage and influence policymakers, industry representatives and other stakeholders at the highest level.

Contract Duration, Location, Remuneration
• Duration: This is a one-year consultancy contract, with a high possibility of conversion to a full-time position upon successful completion of the term and depending on future project needs.

• Work Arrangement: [e.g., Consultant Contract/Flexible arrangement, including required travel for meetings/data gathering.

• The salary package and title depends on experience. We are an equal opportunities employer and offer competitive salary and benefits.

About T&E
T&E is the independent expert in enabling clean transport for all. Our vision is a zero-emissions mobility system that is affordable and has minimal impacts on our health and environment. Since we were created 30 years ago, T&E has shaped some of Europe’s most important environmental laws. We got the EU to set the world's most ambitious CO2 standards for cars and trucks but also helped uncover the Dieselgate scandal; we campaigned successfully to end palm oil diesel, secured a global ban on dirty shipping fuels and the creation of the aviation ETS, the world's largest carbon market for aviation, to name just a few.

We combine the power of robust, science-based evidence and a deep understanding of transport with powerful communications and impactful advocacy. Our staff in Brussels, Paris, Rome, Madrid, Berlin, Warsaw and London collaborate with our 49 national members. From 2024, T&E has been enhancing our collaboration between Asia and Europe, starting from our Singapore office, to accelerate zero-emission transport and energy transition, helping ensure that global decarbonization efforts are both inclusive and regionally grounded. Altogether, our members represent more than 3.5 million people.

Protecting Your Personal Data against Recruitment Scams: T&E takes digital data privacy and information security seriously. Please note that all legitimate communication from our talent acquisition team will exclusively originate from an official corporate domain ending in @transportenvironment.org (or cleancitiescampaign.org) or directly via secure automated channels on our managed applicant tracking platform.

• No Unverified Communication: T&E does not authorize external recruitment agencies or headhunters to contact candidates using unverified, generic webmail accounts such as @gmail.com, @yahoo.com, or @outlook.com.

• No Charging or Fees: T&E will never request sensitive financial information, banking credentials, passport copies, or any form of payment at any stage of our recruitment process.

• Verification Protocol: All legitimate T&E vacancies are listed on our 2 websites https://jobs.transportenvironment.org/ or https://cleancitiescampaign.org/vacancies/

If you receive a suspicious solicitation and wish to verify its legitimacy, please cross-reference the vacancy on our 2 websites or forward the communication directly to the HR team at hrsupport@transportenvironment.org before sharing any personal documentation.

raw.job_description:
AI時代の新しい産業体験をデザインする｜プロダクトデザイナー（UI/UX）

Description

なぜ、リアル産業にUXデザインが必要なのか？

建設業や製造業では今なお、

・電話

・メール

・Excel

・紙図面

を中心としたコミュニケーションが数多く残っています。

多くの業務は、人の経験や暗黙知によって支えられています。

しかしAI時代に求められるのは、単なるデジタル化ではありません。

複雑な業務を理解し、

情報の流れを整理し、

人とテクノロジーが自然に協働できる体験を設計することです。

BALLASのデザイナーは、単に画面をデザインするだけではありません。

設計・調達・製造・施工にまたがる業務を理解しながら、新しい産業体験そのものを設計していく存在です。

業務内容

BALLASのデザイナーは、プロダクトだけでなく事業やブランドも含めた体験設計を担います。

プロダクトデザイン

• 顧客業務の観察・課題発見
• ユーザー体験設計
• 情報設計
• UIデザイン
• デザインシステム構築
• PdMやエンジニアとのプロダクト開発

サービスデザイン

• 設計、調達、施工など業務プロセスの可視化
• 顧客接点全体の体験設計
• 新規プロダクトのコンセプト設計

ブランドデザイン

• サービスサイト
• コーポレートサイト
• 営業資料
• ホワイトペーパー
• イベントクリエイティブ など、プロダクトとブランドを横断した体験づくりを担います。

BALLASとは？

「建設業を最適化し、人々を幸せに。」をミッションに掲げ、建設サプライチェーンをアップグレードするテックカンパニーです。

プラットフォーム運営を通じて設計・調達・製造に携わりながら一次情報を蓄積し、業界の標準化・最適化を推進しています。

リアルなオペレーションをコード化し、AI Nativeな産業インフラの構築を目指しています。

BALLASのプロダクト

BALLASでは「BALLAS SCM」と「BALLAS LINKS」の2つのプロダクトがあります。

「BALLAS SCM」は、自社とパートナー工場様が使うサービスで、設計から製造までのオペレーションをAI Nativeに再設計するためのプロダクトです。

「BALLAS LINKS」は、お客様である建設工事会社様が使うプロダクトです。こちらは、建設工事会社様の内部にある設計・調達プロセスを統合するプロジェクト基盤になります。

今までお客様は、図面の管理にファイルサーバーやクラウド、仕様の協議はメールやチャット、やりとりは口頭と様々なツールを使い分ける状況でした。それを一つに統合することで、認識のズレや余計な工数を大幅に削減できます。さらに、蓄積された作図・購買プロセスデータをもとに、AIによる業務の自動化も進めています。

【参考：BALLASが取り組む課題】

BALLASが挑む建設サプライチェーンの復興──消えゆく町工場と日本の課題

https://youtrust.jp/studio/articles/ballas

代表・木村の起業への想い

なぜBALLASを立ち上げたのか

1400年以上にわたり日本の発展を支えてきた建設業界は、今なお社会インフラを支える巨大産業です。一方で、現場では深刻な職人不足や、アナログで不透明な調達プロセスによる過度な調整負担など、産業全体の生産性を阻害する課題が残されています。

多重請負構造の中で分断されてきた設計・調達・製造・施工のプロセスをデータでつなぎ直し、人とAIが協働できる業務構造へ再設計することで、人が創造的な仕事や本質的な意思決定に集中できる産業を実現したい。

その想いから、BALLASを創業しました。

BALLASが目指すのは、顧客・パートナーにDXを強制しないDXです。

建設部材の調達プラットフォーム「BALLAS」は、自らがサプライヤーとして設計・調達・製造に携わりながら一次情報を蓄積し、業界の標準化・最適化を推進しています。「BALLASに頼めば、やり方を変えずに業務が最適化されていく」そんな体験を提供していきたいと考えています。

【参考：サプライヤーBALLASという戦略】

■取締役COO中西「川下から川上へ、サプライチェーンをかえる」

https://note.com/ballas/n/nd8f29e3d2c54

BALLASという組織の3つの魅力

① 産業変革の最前線で、事業と組織の両方をつくるフェーズ

IPOを目指す成長過程にありながら、事業・組織ともに未完成。

仕組みづくりや新たな挑戦の機会が数多くあります。

② AI Nativeな働き方を実践する組織

Claude Code、Cursor、Devin、Gemini などの生成AIツールを組織の標準装備として活用しています

AIを個人の工夫に留めず、組織の生産性向上につなげる取り組みを推進しています。

共同創業者 執行役員 コーポレート本部 責任者益田の記事

Thales is a global technology leader trusted by governments, institutions, and enterprises to tackle their most demanding challenges. From quantum applications and artificial intelligence to cybersecurity and 6G innovation, our solutions empower critical decisions rooted in human intelligence. Operating at the forefront of aerospace and space, cybersecurity and digital identity, we’re driven by a mission to build a future we can all trust.

Thales has been present in the Republic of Indonesia for 45 years in the defence, aerospace and space domains, delivering a wide range of civil and defence solutions that highlight our strong commitment to working with the Indonesian government and local stakeholders. In recent years, our innovative solutions in air traffic management systems and telecom satellites have further strengthened our presence in the country alongside our digital portfolio of solutions such as biometrics, data protection and cybersecurity now serving the needs of diverse customers in civil sectors.

As a Network & Security Infrastructure Engineer, you will be part of the Internet and Cloud Access Squad and actively contribute to various projects and tasks related to critical infrastructures.

Your main missions will include:

• Infrastructure Projects: Collaborate with the team to design, implement, and maintain network infrastructures, with a focus on Proxies, Sandbox, and Firewall systems.
• Operational Support: Assist in resolving network-related incidents and contribute to proactive performance monitoring of the network.
• Optimization & Security: Contribute to the continuous improvement of network-related processes and tools while ensuring security and compliance of network environments.
• Documentation & Reporting: Maintain accurate documentation of network configurations, operational procedures, and resolved incidents. Produce periodic reports on network performance and trends.
• Agile Collaboration: Participate in Agile team meetings, share progress and obstacles, and contribute to collaborative problem-solving.

Technical Skills:
• You can define and implement network requirements across various production processes.
• You have strong analytical skills and provide real expertise in Level 3 support.
• You can configure network and security equipment and other IT assets, including:• Proxies: Skyhigh (formerly McAfee), Zscaler, SSL inspection, Whitelist/Blacklist management, URL categorization, web filtering, content filtering, CAS.
• Sandbox: Trellix (formerly McAfee), Zscaler.

• You have a strong appetite for automation, backed by solid skills in programming languages: Curl, PowerShell, Python, Bash.

• Cloud Security: SASE, Zero Trust Network Access (ZTNA), DLP, CASB, SD-WAN, SWG.
• Directories: Active Directory, LDAPS.
• IAM (Identity & Access Management): Kerberos, SAML, Single Sign-On (SSO), Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA).
